operator_plays.name: Subject-To Low-Rate Mortgage Acquisition & RMLO-Underwritten Wraparound Note Spread Arbitrage
operator_plays.mechanism: Acquire property subject to existing 2.75%–4.25% mortgage debt and, where lawful, resell through an 8.5%–9.9% wraparound note originated with licensed RMLO involvement, applicable ability-to-repay review and licensed third-party servicing. Retain lawful origination economics and the net interest spread rather than operating as a landlord. RMLO involvement does not eliminate due-on-sale acceleration, seller liability, buyer default or property-related obligations.
inputs: Verified underlying loan, title, tax and insurance records with seller disclosures and counsel-reviewed due-on-sale analysis
Qualified buyer file and licensed RMLO underwriting with applicable SAFE Act, Dodd-Frank and state wraparound compliance
Legally reviewed transfer and wrap documents plus licensed third-party servicing, payment verification and default reserves
workflow: 1. Verify the underlying mortgage and title, disclose the seller's continuing debt exposure and obtain counsel-reviewed lender consent or a documented lawful acceleration-risk plan.
2. Underwrite the buyer through a licensed RMLO where required and deliver all applicable consumer, financing and wraparound disclosures.
3. Close only a lawful documented transfer with appropriate insurance and escrow arrangements, assigning property responsibilities explicitly rather than assuming none exist.
4. Service the wrap through a licensed third party, verify underlying debt and tax payments monthly and follow lawful loss-mitigation procedures if payments fail.
metrics: Collected wrap interest less underlying interest, servicing fees and credit-loss provision
Buyer delinquency rate and percentage of underlying payments verified on time
Liquidity reserves relative to acceleration, foreclosure and property carrying exposure

platform_risks.failure_mode: The underlying lender accelerates debt after a subject-to transfer
platform_risks.trigger: Enforcement of a due-on-sale clause or a related servicing or insurance default
platform_risks.impact: Immediate payoff demand, refinancing costs, foreclosure exposure and harm to the original borrower
platform_risks.detection_metric: Lender acceleration notices, unresolved servicing alerts and reserve shortfall against payoff exposure
platform_risks.fallback: Engage counsel and the servicer, pursue lender-approved assumption or refinancing and use a documented lawful sale or payoff exit if necessary

operator_plays.name: Distressed Asset Recovery
operator_plays.mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.
inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers
Unclaimed property & judgment dockets
Surplus auction manifests
workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances
Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value
Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts
metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case
Claim approval rate
Days from filing to disbursement

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold
platform_risks.trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules
platform_risks.impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle
platform_risks.detection_metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance
platform_risks.fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required

operator_plays.name: Probate Docket & Pre-Foreclosure Notice-of-Default (NOD) Scraping
operator_plays.mechanism: Parse county probate petitions (Letters Testamentary / Letters of Administration) and daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) filings before national aggregators index them, matching out-of-state personal representatives and distressed owners to licensed probate brokers and cash buyers.
inputs: County probate court register of actions & Letters Testamentary filings
County recorder daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) & Notice-of-Trustee-Sale feeds
Skip-tracing & out-of-state personal-representative matching pipeline
workflow: Extract newly appointed estate personal representatives and real-property inventory from county probate dockets within 24 hours of filing
Cross-match parcel equity and mortgage balances against county assessor and recorder records
Deliver empathetic estate-liquidation checklists, property-preservation referrals, or licensed brokerage introductions
metrics: Docket-to-first-contact speed vs. national data aggregators (days)
Personal-representative response & appointment rate (%)
Commission or referral fee per closed probate/pre-foreclosure parcel

platform_risks.failure_mode: State Foreclosure Consultant Act violations or unlicensed brokerage fee-splitting
platform_risks.trigger: Charging upfront fees to distressed homeowners in NOD or taking unlicensed real-estate commission splits
platform_risks.impact: Voided contracts, treble damages under state foreclosure-protection statutes, or DRE enforcement
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% licensed broker co-marketing compliance and zero upfront homeowner fee charges
platform_risks.fallback: Monetize strictly via flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions to licensed probate agents or close transactions through a licensed brokerage of record

operator_plays.name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage
operator_plays.mechanism: Price small HOA priority liens and tax-sale interests using jurisdiction-specific priority, notice, and redemption rules; returns depend on enforceable rights, not assumed title extinguishment.
inputs: County tax-sale and HOA lien records
Title report and statutory redemption calendar
Local counsel priority and notice opinion
workflow: 1. Screen small-balance liens against property value, senior debt, and sale eligibility
2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions
3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline
4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire
metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs
Capital days outstanding
Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien
platform_risks.trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority
platform_risks.impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests

Dispatch transparent, non-governmental trigger mailers within 24–48 hours of filing with personalized QR codes pre-populating entity or parcel data

operator_plays.name: Automated Commercial/Residential Property-Tax Appeal Arbitrage
operator_plays.mechanism: Ingest county tax-assessor valuation rolls upon annual notice release, run an automated valuation model (AVM) flagging parcels assessed above comparable neighbor equity ratios, and file bulk administrative tax protests for 30–50% of the first year's verified tax reduction.

Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine

operator_plays.name: Earnest-Money Deposit ("Gator") Escrow Lending & Joint-Venture Splits
operator_plays.mechanism: Advance $2,500–$25,000 refundable-contingency earnest-money deposits directly to title escrow under documented JV or promissory protections, with security recorded or perfected where legally appropriate. Negotiate a 15%–30% share of an earned assignment fee or a lawful fixed return; refunds depend on contractual deadlines, valid contingency exercise and escrow release terms.
inputs: Assignable purchase agreement with explicit refundable contingencies, notice procedures and deadline calendar
Verified title escrow account and executed JV or promissory documents with legally appropriate recorded or perfected protections
Borrower diligence, assignment economics and state-specific lending, brokerage, securities and usury review
workflow: 1. Verify assignment rights, counterparty identity, refundable contingencies and the enforceability of the proposed JV or lending structure.
2. Execute repayment and profit-split documents, perfect any lawful security and transmit the deposit directly to verified title escrow.
3. Track contingency and assignment deadlines, require documented progress and deliver timely cancellation notices when authorized and necessary.
4. Reconcile the closing or refund statement, recover deposited principal and collect only the contractually earned fee or lawful return.
metrics: Earned assignment-fee share or fixed return per completed deposit advance
Percentage of active deposits with verified unexpired refund rights and complete documentation
Deposit loss rate and median days from advance to cleared repayment

platform_risks.trigger: Missed contingency notice deadline, invalid cancellation or unauthorized contract amendment
platform_risks.impact: Deposit forfeiture, delayed recovery and disputes over assignment proceeds
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deposits approaching contingency expiry without documented assignment or cancellation instructions
platform_risks.fallback: Freeze additional advances, seek timely authorized cancellation and pursue counsel-reviewed escrow release or contractual remedies

operator_plays.name: 24-to-72-Hour Escrow-Locked Transactional ("Flash") Double-Close Funding
operator_plays.mechanism: Fund the A->B acquisition only after the title agent independently verifies cleared, unconditional end-buyer B->C funds in escrow and an enforceable closing waterfall. Target a 1.0%–2.5% earned funding fee per 1–3 day turn; closing delays, fraud and legal restrictions can impair returns or principal.

Cleared end-buyer escrow funds, written disbursement conditions and a reconciled same-transaction payoff waterfall
Commercial-purpose funding agreement reviewed for applicable licensing, usury and escrow requirements
workflow: 1. Underwrite both contracts, title exceptions, end-buyer closing conditions and the settlement agent's authority and applicable bonding or insurance.
2. Independently confirm end-buyer cleared funds and irrevocable disbursement instructions using a previously verified title-agent contact channel.
3. Wire A->B funding only to approved title escrow after all release conditions are satisfied and the closing sequence is documented.
4. Reconcile B->C settlement, recover principal and earned fees, and release capital for reuse only after cleared repayment is confirmed.

Median and maximum hours from funding disbursement to cleared repayment
Unrecovered principal and delayed-closing exposure as a percentage of outstanding funding

platform_risks.failure_mode: Fraudulent wire instructions or conditional end-buyer funds leave the A->B advance unrepaid
platform_risks.trigger: Last-minute beneficiary changes, failed independent callbacks or unresolved B->C release conditions
platform_risks.impact: Loss of principal, prolonged escrow disputes and interruption of capital recycling
platform_risks.detection_metric: Count of unresolved wire-verification exceptions and funded closings past contractual repayment deadlines
platform_risks.fallback: Stop disbursement, independently reverify settlement instructions and obtain counsel-directed escrow recovery before further funding

positioning_alternatives.title: The Low-Rate Debt Spread Desk
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Acquire subject to existing debt, price acceleration exposure, and retain documented wraparound payment spreads.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Experienced residential operators with title counsel, licensed RMLO relationships, and liquidity beyond the initial setup budget.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 generally permits enforcement of contractual due-on-sale provisions, subject to enumerated limitations. A routine investor acquisition is not automatically an exempt transfer. The operating edge therefore depends on verified debt terms, transparent transfer documentation, and a credible payoff or refinance response.

positioning_alternatives.title: The RMLO-Underwritten Wraparound Desk
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Build owner-occupant wrap transactions around documented repayment capacity, state licensing, and transaction-specific disclosures.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Small real estate teams prepared to use licensed origination professionals rather than treating seller exemptions as a shortcut.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: 12 U.S.C. §§5102–5103 establish SAFE Act definitions and licensing or registration requirements. Regulation Z, 12 CFR §§1026.36 and 1026.43, governs relevant origination conduct and repayment-capacity requirements within its scope. The operating policy sends every owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO; counsel documents transaction coverage and any applicable exemption. Texas Property Code §5.016 and Finance Code Chapter 159 require separate analysis.

positioning_alternatives.title: The Servicer-Verified Note Spread Pod
positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Run a four-person core operation around verified collections, underlying mortgage payments, and tax-and-insurance reconciliation.
positioning_alternatives.audience: Portfolio operators who value payment evidence, exception handling, and retained contribution more than property-face-value headlines.
positioning_alternatives.research_basis: Regulation X servicing provisions, including 12 CFR §§1024.17, 1024.35, and 1024.41 where applicable, identify concrete escrow, error-resolution, and loss-mitigation responsibilities. A licensed third-party servicer provides the operating rail; the operator still reconciles receipts and underlying payments. Texas Finance Code Chapter 159 adds wrap-specific requirements for covered loans.

chapters.question_prompt: What exactly is subject-to & wraparound note arbitrage, how is real operator revenue recognized vs underlying asset/client GMV, and what separates durable small-team moats from fragile beginner hype?
chapters.title: What Exactly Is Subject-To & Wraparound Note Arbitrage?
chapters.subtitle: Low-Rate Debt, RMLO-Underwritten Wrap Notes, Garn-St Germain Transfer Risk, and Licensed-Servicer Cash Waterfalls
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #35, Subject-To & Wraparound Note Arbitrage, ranks #09 of 36 with a 90/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. The operator acquires property subject to existing low-rate debt, then finances a qualified buyer through a lawful wraparound note. Revenue means retained upfront economics and interest spread, never property value or debt-service throughput. This chapter organizes 11 mapped plays: two specified cross-shelf plays and nine supporting operating applications. Canonical annual owner profits are $28,000 Conservative, $190,000 Base, and $442,000 Scaled. Durable returns require licensed RMLO underwriting, licensed third-party servicing, verified underlying payments, and a funded acceleration exit. The moat is a documented performing-note system; a large coupon without transfer-risk reserves is merely leveraged exposure.

sections.heading: 1. Acquire a financing position, not an exemption from mortgage risk
paragraphs: Subject-to describes a title acquisition in which an existing mortgage remains attached to the property and the original borrower ordinarily remains liable on the underlying note. It is not a lender-approved assumption, and making payments does not release that borrower. A wraparound resale creates a new buyer obligation that includes the economic burden of the existing debt. The operator collects the wrap payment through a licensed third-party servicer, funds the underlying obligation, and retains the permitted spread after expenses. The specified play, subject_to_wraparound_rmlo_note_spread, targets underlying coupons of 2.75%–4.25% and buyer coupons of 8.5%–9.9%, subject to underwriting, pricing restrictions, and state execution rules. Those bands describe a screening thesis, not an entitlement to charge any particular borrower a particular rate. Start with the actual note, security instrument, payment history, payoff statement, title commitment, insurance declarations, and escrow analysis. A seller's dashboard screenshot cannot establish lien priority, reinstatement cost, or permission to transfer. Record who owns the property, who owes each debt, who services each payment, and who can enforce each remedy. These relationships determine whether the apparent spread survives a missed payment, casualty loss, lender demand, or disputed closing.

The simplest unit illustration uses a $200,000 underlying balance at 3.5% and a $220,000 wrap balance at 9.0%. Opening-balance annualized interest is $7,000 underneath and $19,800 on the wrap, producing $12,800 before servicing, losses, carrying costs, and overhead. This is an interest snapshot, not a twelve-month amortization forecast. Calculate actual monthly interest on declining balances and split every payment between principal, interest, escrow, and charges. If the resale price is $240,000 and the buyer contributes $20,000, the resulting $220,000 note fits that illustration; neither the $240,000 price nor the entire down payment becomes retained operating revenue. Compare the scheduled underlying payment with the buyer's fully underwritten housing payment, including taxes, insurance, association charges, and applicable assessments. Reject a structure that works only because escrow shortages or repairs are ignored. A $45 monthly servicing budget consumes $540 annually; an additional $2,400 operating reserve allocation reduces distributable cash further, although transferring cash to a reserve is not itself an accounting expense. If acceleration occurs, engage counsel and the servicer, seek lender-approved assumption or refinancing, and execute a documented lawful sale or payoff when necessary.

Five operator archetypes share the same payment plumbing but require different acquisition discipline. A low-equity seller specialist solves a narrow exit problem; an equity-rich seller specialist must separately fund the seller's equity rather than pretend a cheap first mortgage finances everything. An owner-occupant wrap originator needs a qualified buyer and documented repayment capacity. A performing-note operator earns through collected cash flows rather than repeated closings. An institutional process specialist supplies servicing oversight and evidence management without representing that administration transfers creditor obligations. Use PropStream or ATTOM to identify candidate properties, then verify ownership and recorded liens through authoritative county records and a title professional. Low-equity and pre-foreclosure signals are research inputs, not invitations to pressure distressed households. Map state foreclosure-rescue restrictions before discussing a transaction with an owner facing an active sale date. The practical moat is a network of title personnel, RMLOs, servicers, insurance agents, and local counsel who can reject defective transactions quickly. The beginner mistake is building marketing volume before establishing this rejection capability. One disputed deed or uninsurable transfer can consume several years of modeled interest margin and strand the original borrower.

callout.title: Underwrite the documents that survive a bad month
callout.body: A useful acquisition file explains the downside without requiring the original salesperson to interpret it.
items: Obtain a current reinstatement or payoff statement directly through authorized channels; reconcile legal fees and escrow advances before pricing seller proceeds.
Compare the underlying amortization schedule with the proposed wrap schedule month by month; a favorable coupon gap can conceal an unfavorable payment gap.
Require the insurance agent to document ownership, occupancy, mortgagee interests, and loss-payee treatment accurately rather than preserve an obsolete policy description.
Keep an acceleration-exit worksheet with dated refinance assumptions, sale costs, liens, and available liquidity; refresh it whenever value or borrower performance deteriorates.

sections.heading: 2. Separate asset value, cash collections, retained revenue, and owner profit
paragraphs: The scorecard's gross revenue field uses a deliberately narrow economic boundary: net upfront option or down-payment spreads plus retained annual wraparound interest margin. It excludes home face value, mortgage principal collections, escrow receipts, and pass-through debt service. Treat that boundary as a management reporting convention, not a substitute for transaction-specific accounting. A property sale, loan origination, purchased note, and separately contracted administrative service can follow different recognition rules. Interest-bearing instruments are generally analyzed under applicable financial-instrument guidance rather than automatically applying ASC 606 to every receipt. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis matters where a service arrangement actually falls within its scope. A buyer's down payment can represent purchase consideration, principal recovery, deferred amounts, or refundable funds; it is not automatically earned fee income. Build a closing statement bridge that identifies seller proceeds, lien cures, third-party charges, refundable balances, basis recovery, and any amount actually eligible for recognition. Have the accountant reconcile the scorecard presentation to the financial statements. Do not apply another retained-share haircut to scorecard dollars already expressed on a retained basis. Equally, never inflate those dollars by adding the mortgage payments handled for somebody else.

The canonical Conservative case is $100,000 revenue, $72,000 expenses, and $28,000 annual owner profit at 28%. Base is $475,000 revenue, $285,000 expenses, and $190,000 profit at 40.0%. Scaled is $850,000 revenue, $408,000 expenses, and $442,000 profit at 52%. Staffing remains one full-time operator plus three contractors in the first two cases and two full-time operators plus four contractors in the third. These are the fixed Formula v2.0 outputs, not projections derived from the single-property illustration. A transparent illustrative bridge uses $25,000 retained upfront economics plus $75,000 retained interest for Conservative; $175,000 plus $300,000 for Base; and $300,000 plus $550,000 for Scaled. The bridge reconciles revenue but does not assert an undocumented portfolio count or closing cadence. Recurring overhead of $2,000–$12,000 monthly is only one component of total expenses. Direct origination work, acquisition expenses, servicing, collection costs, realized losses, and other properly recognized charges explain why annual total expenses can exceed that overhead range. Keep owner distributions, debt principal, and cash reserve transfers outside the expense bridge unless their underlying accounting treatment requires otherwise. Avoid subtracting underlying interest twice after reporting interest margin net of that same cost.

Startup capital of $12,000–$65,000 and a two-to-six-month first-deal window describe access conditions, not sufficient capitalization for every acquisition. A property requiring $18,000 of reinstatement, $7,000 of closing and repair cash, and $10,000 of liquidity already absorbs $35,000 before any seller equity payment. An $800,000 portfolio balance does not become operating revenue merely because the operator controls its payment instructions. Build separate ledgers for property basis, underlying debt, wrap receivables, escrow liabilities, retained income, and unrestricted cash. Use QuickBooks Online for the general ledger and a licensed servicer's loan-level statements for contractual balances; neither should silently overwrite the other. Reconcile bank deposits to collection batches, batches to borrower statements, and underlying remittances to lender confirmations. A principal collection improves cash availability while reducing a receivable; interest recognition and loss provisioning require their own analysis. Stress liquidity for borrower delinquency, tax reassessment, insurance renewal, legal expense, and an accelerated first mortgage. The largest downside is often a payoff demand rather than one missed installment. Profit quality therefore depends on funded survival time and exit feasibility, not only the percentage printed beside the annual revenue figure.

sections.heading: 3. Compare sixteen sub-verticals and map eleven executable operating plays
paragraphs: The comparison matrix distinguishes eleven mapped operating plays from five additional underwriting segments. Plays one and eleven use the two supplied cross-shelf identifiers; plays two through ten are descriptive operating applications, not invented catalog identifiers. Play one is the complete subject-to wrap engine. The nine supporting applications cover low-equity sourcing, arrears resolution, seller-equity funding, buyer qualification, servicing, escrow auditing, performing-note retention, workouts, and acceleration exits. Their unit economics are costs, capital allocations, or retained receipts within the same transaction, not eleven independent revenue streams. The five additional segments expose different risks involving condominiums, insurance, tax resets, balloons, and note sales. Named platforms identify practical research or workflow tools, not endorsements or verified current price quotations. Every dollar budget in the matrix is an illustrative operator assumption to replace with a written quote. PropStream and ATTOM can support sourcing; ICE Mortgage Technology Encompass can support an RMLO's origination workflow; DocuSign can document permitted electronic execution. None establishes that a particular transfer, instrument, fee, or foreclosure remedy is valid. A title professional and state-specific execution plan remain necessary even when the software shows a complete checklist.

The second specified play, tcpa_litigator_scrub_honeypot_arbitrage, is best understood here as consent-first outbound risk screening, not a method for bypassing telephone restrictions. Lawfully obtained PACER or CourtListener records can contribute docket-derived risk signals alongside authoritative do-not-call checks, revocation processing, identity verification, and channel-specific consent evidence. A plaintiff match neither authorizes contact nor establishes that someone is a fraudulent claimant. Name collisions, stale telephone assignments, sealed records, and incomplete dockets create obvious error paths. For a separately contracted screening service, an illustrative $0.03 charge on 10,000 authorized screening events yields $300 billings; $120 of data and processing costs leaves $180 contribution before labor and overhead. Those amounts do not enter the canonical real-estate scenario bridge. Price the service for evidence preservation and suppression accuracy, not a promise of immunity. Apply 47 U.S.C. §227, 47 CFR §64.1200, applicable state calling rules, and the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule where relevant. Disable uncertain enrichment and require independently verified consent and authoritative suppression checks when provenance or matching fails. Never rotate numbers or change vendors to defeat a recipient's revocation.

Evaluate every sub-vertical using the same four questions: what money is actually retained, what capital remains exposed, what document proves performance, and what event reverses the expected economics? A $2,000 closing fee can be less valuable than $600 of well-supported annual contribution if the former carries a refund obligation or conceals defective origination. Conversely, a long-duration note with an attractive coupon can be worth little when its underlying mortgage is immediately callable and no exit is funded. Record refund and repurchase obligations as contract terms, not generic worst-case language. In a note sale, distinguish sale proceeds and carrying value from previously recognized interest; representations about payment history can create recourse after cash arrives. For condominium and association properties, read assessment notices and lien provisions before calculating the buyer's housing burden. For insurance-sensitive properties, obtain a bound or bindable coverage plan reflecting actual ownership and occupancy. For balloon structures, test lawful availability and repayment feasibility rather than assume refinancing. The comparison favors repeatable document quality over exotic terms: an ordinary fixed-payment transaction with reliable remittances usually fits a small team better than a clever instrument requiring constant exceptions and emergency legal work.

sections.heading: 4. Build a small-team control system that survives acceleration and default
paragraphs: Federal due-on-sale law is the first structural constraint. Under 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3, lenders generally may enforce contractual due-on-sale provisions subject to specified protections and exceptions. An ordinary investor acquisition does not automatically qualify for those protections. A trust label, payment history, or servicing arrangement does not independently neutralize acceleration. Explain continuing seller liability and record the agreed response to a lender demand. For Texas property, Tex. Prop. Code §5.016 addresses notice requirements for certain conveyances encumbered by recorded liens, with statutory exceptions; Texas Finance Code Chapter 159 separately addresses wrap mortgage loan licensing, disclosures, and related obligations. Treat these as distinct analyses rather than one universal form. For owner-occupant buyers, require licensed RMLO involvement as the operating standard, then determine applicable federal and state creditor, originator, disclosure, and ability-to-repay duties. The SAFE Act framework, 12 U.S.C. §§5101–5116, does not replace Regulation Z analysis. Seller-financer exclusions under 12 CFR §1026.36 have conditions and limited scope; they do not automatically eliminate obligations under §1026.43. Resolve coverage before advertising terms, collecting application fees, or promising a closing date to the buyer.

A one-person operator should coordinate specialists, not impersonate all of them. In the Conservative and Base team design, the three contractor roles cover transaction and legal coordination, licensed origination, and licensed servicing or bookkeeping coordination. Required title, insurance, and other vendors remain external service providers; the staffing shorthand is not a claim that three people hold every necessary credential. At Scaled, a second full-time operator owns portfolio exceptions while four contractors support repeatable execution. Build a monthly evidence packet containing buyer collections, underlying lender confirmations, escrow movements, tax and insurance status, delinquencies, and current reserve availability. Use the servicer's controlled portal for sensitive records and restricted accounting access for reconciliation. Avoid emailing complete identity documents across a casual deal group. Separate payment authorization from reconciliation wherever practical, even if that separation is an external bookkeeper checking the owner's instructions. Route exceptions by severity: insurance cancellation and acceleration notices outrank routine document cleanup. A shared calendar tracks notice deadlines, renewal dates, escrow reviews, and note maturities. Automation should collect evidence and expose exceptions; it should not independently issue legal notices or change borrower terms without authorized professional review.

The final purchase decision combines profitability with survivability. Require a positive retained spread after realistic servicing and loss assumptions, a buyer payment supported by verified capacity, accurate insurance, a lawful closing path, and an executable response to acceleration. A six-month reserve based on $1,600 of monthly underlying payment and $400 of property carrying costs equals $12,000, but it does not fund a $200,000 payoff demand. Track those risks separately. If a buyer defaults, contact the servicer and counsel, preserve records, evaluate permitted workouts, and follow applicable notice and foreclosure procedures. Do not use lockouts, utility interruption, or informal repossession as collection tools. If the underlying lender accelerates, confirm the demand and deadlines, update payoff figures, evaluate lender-approved assumption or refinancing, and prepare a lawful sale if necessary. The seller should receive the communications promised in the transaction documents rather than discover problems through damaged credit. Review portfolio concentration by underlying lender, geography, insurance exposure, maturity date, and servicer. The durable small-team business earns a financing spread while continuously verifying performance; the fragile version spends upfront cash and hopes nobody exercises a contractual right.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #35, Subject-To & Wraparound Note Arbitrage, ranks #09 of 36 with a 90/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Across 11 mapped plays, the commercial test is identical: identify the authorized payer, document the earned spread, and reconcile collected cash to enforceable obligations. This chapter develops that test through owner-occupant wraps and the distressed_asset_recovery bridge. Sellers seek an executable exit; buyers pay for ownership through documented financing; neither motive excuses weak underwriting or concealed transfers. Formula v2.0 produces annual owner profits of $28,000, $190,000, and $442,000 on recognized operator revenue of $100,000, $475,000, and $850,000. Licensed origination, independent settlement, verified underlying payments, and segregated tax and insurance funds turn a quoted interest spread into collectible operating income.

sections.heading: 1. Identify the payer, the pressure, and the person authorized to release money
paragraphs: The wrap buyer writes the recurring check, while the property seller usually contributes an opportunity rather than a recurring fee. A low-equity seller may face a mortgage cure deadline, relocation costs, vacancy expenses, or a sale price insufficient to cover conventional brokerage and settlement charges. Their decision is whether a documented transfer improves their position relative to a negotiated lender workout or ordinary sale. Buying subject to an existing mortgage does not automatically release that seller from personal liability. Put that continuing exposure, the payment-monitoring arrangement, and the lender's acceleration rights into the transaction discussion before requesting signatures. The buyer's pressure is different: they want an affordable home and a financing path their documented income can support. A thin credit file or unconventional employment history is a reason to investigate repayment capacity, not permission to skip it. Ask what monthly housing payment remains affordable after taxes, insurance, association dues, and ordinary living obligations. Neither impending foreclosure nor bank rejection creates payment capacity. The operator earns a spread only when these two situations can be matched without selling either party a hidden obligation.

Authority follows the asset and the account, not the loudest participant on a sales call. Confirm every record owner, required spouse signature, entity manager, trustee, and estate representative before treating a seller's acceptance as executable. Obtain the underlying borrower's written authorization for lender communications and statement access; that authorization is not lender consent to the transfer. The settlement agent controls closing disbursements under signed instructions, while the licensed servicer controls recurring collections under its servicing agreement. The operator cannot casually redirect either account. On the buyer side, identify who owns the down-payment funds, whether another person is providing a gift, and whether repayment obligations affect underwriting. Verify bank records through approved secure channels and document large recent deposits. A purchase contract with two buyers but funds from an unrelated business requires explanation before closing, not a convenient third-party payment link. For a $20,000 buyer deposit, a signed allocation might direct $12,000 toward seller equity and arrears, $3,000 toward documented acquisition and settlement costs, and $5,000 toward the operator's modeled upfront spread. That allocation describes deal economics; it does not by itself determine the accounting treatment of a down payment.

Counterparty screening must test willingness, capacity, and authority separately. For the seller, examine title, judgment liens, bankruptcy filings, delinquent taxes, association balances, and actual reinstatement figures. A bankruptcy filing can invoke the automatic stay under 11 U.S.C. §362; do not treat a distressed owner's signature as sufficient authority to continue collection or foreclosure activity. For the buyer, use a licensed residential mortgage loan originator, or RMLO, to document income, employment, assets, debts, credit history, and repayment capacity under applicable rules. Apply consistent written criteria rather than neighborhood assumptions or protected characteristics. Consumer reports require a permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. §1681b, and credit decisions can trigger adverse-action duties under Regulation B and the Fair Credit Reporting Act. For the servicer, inspect applicable licenses, trust-account controls, complaint history, continuity plans, and sample reconciliations. For the lender, read the actual security instrument and identify acceleration exposure. The Garn-St Germain exceptions in 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 are specific; an ordinary investor purchase is not automatically protected. Decline the deal when an affordable buyer payment, a defensible transfer structure, and a funded downside plan cannot coexist.

sections.heading: 2. Match each payment to a rail, a release condition, and a reversal risk
paragraphs: A payment rail moves funds; it does not establish entitlement to them. For acquisition and resale closings, use a settlement professional permitted to handle the transaction in the property's jurisdiction. Confirm wire instructions through a previously verified telephone number, never through contact details supplied in an unexpected instruction-change email. Record the callback, beneficiary identity, bank routing information, and the settlement file reference. Release funds only against the signed disbursement statement and the applicable recording and title conditions. A domestic wire generally offers stronger settlement finality than a consumer debit, but a bank's receipt confirmation still does not prove that every contractual condition has been satisfied. Escrow is an account-control and instruction framework, not a separate electronic network. It can receive wires or other permitted funds while restricting who may release them. Likewise, a milestone hold is a contractual release mechanism layered over an account. Keeping these categories distinct prevents a common sales error: describing money as protected merely because a payment application displays a successful transfer. The relevant questions are where the funds sit, who owns them, and which verified event permits disbursement.

Recurring buyer payments should flow to the licensed servicer rather than the operator's general operating account. ACH debits require appropriate authorization and remain exposed to returns and disputes; a settlement date is not universal finality. Regulation E, including 12 CFR §1005.10, governs relevant consumer preauthorized transfers and restricts conditioning credit on repayment by recurring electronic transfers. Offer a workable alternative rather than making autopay the sole route to financing. Require the servicer to define its cutoff times, posting rules, returned-payment treatment, partial-payment handling, and underlying remittance schedule. Build an operating buffer so a late buyer payment does not instantly become a late underlying mortgage payment. For example, three months of a $900 underlying installment requires $2,700 per property before adding taxes, insurance, repairs, or foreclosure expenses. Ten similarly exposed properties require $27,000 just for that installment buffer. Keep this liquidity separate from customer escrow balances. The published $12,000–$65,000 startup range therefore cannot support every portfolio configuration; reserve needs, acquisition cures, and transaction expenses determine the feasible opening size. Automation reduces missed tasks but does not supply missing cash.

The remaining rails are useful mainly because they reveal what should not fund a wrap. A professional retainer pays for a defined engagement and follows the applicable trust-account and earned-fee rules; it is not a substitute for buyer escrow. Statutory disbursement sends proceeds through a court, county, or state process and follows that process's claimant verification, waiting periods, and fee restrictions. A platform checkout may collect an eligible service charge, but card chargebacks, processor restrictions, and account freezes make it a poor default for mortgage installments or property down payments. Check Stripe or PayPal terms for the precise activity instead of assuming ordinary merchant onboarding permits real-estate funds. Factoring monetizes eligible receivables by selling them at a discount; selling a mortgage note instead requires separate transfer, lien, servicing, and investor analysis. Neither route cures a weak borrower. A milestone hold can reserve $2,000 pending an agreed repair inspection when the contract, account structure, and local rules permit it. Specify the inspector, completion standard, dispute procedure, and release deadline. Never withhold an underlying mortgage installment as leverage over an unrelated fee dispute or repair disagreement.

sections.heading: 3. Protect the earned spread without confusing collections, principal, and revenue
paragraphs: Start the ledger with the difference between collection volume and operator revenue. Consider an illustrative opening month with a $200,000 wrap balance at 5.4% and a $180,000 underlying balance at 4.0%. Opening-month interest is $900 on the wrap and $600 on the underlying debt. If the respective contractual principal and interest installments are $1,200 and $900, each reduces its balance by $300 that month. Add a separate $250 buyer escrow collection for taxes and insurance, assuming those amounts are not already included in the underlying installment. The servicer receives $1,450, sends $900 to the underlying lender, allocates $250 to escrow, and charges a $50 servicing fee. The remaining $250 is cash before other expenses and reserves. Retained interest revenue is $300, with the $50 servicing charge treated here as an operating expense. Neither the $300 principal collection nor the $250 escrow receipt becomes revenue. Recalculate later months from actual amortization schedules; equal principal reductions in this opening example do not establish a permanent relationship. This waterfall illustrates mechanics rather than a prescribed consumer loan design or a substitute for originator underwriting.

The canonical Formula v2.0 cases use annual operator revenue of $100,000, $475,000, and $850,000, not home sales volume or aggregate borrower payments. One illustrative reconciliation uses $5,000 of earned net upfront spread per completed transaction and $1,000 of retained annual interest revenue per performing note-year. Conservative activity is ten completions plus fifty note-years: $50,000 plus $50,000 equals $100,000. Base activity is fifty-five completions plus two hundred note-years: $275,000 plus $200,000 equals $475,000. Scaled activity is one hundred completions plus three hundred fifty note-years: $500,000 plus $350,000 equals $850,000. These are alternative portfolio assumptions, not annualizations of the preceding monthly example. A note-year measures time-weighted performing exposure; two notes performing for six months contribute one combined note-year. Existing inventory can therefore exceed current-year closings. Annual operating costs of $72,000, $285,000, and $408,000 leave exact owner profits of $28,000, $190,000, and $442,000. The corresponding margins are 28%, 40.0%, and 52%. The teams remain 1 FT + 3 C, 1 FT + 3 C, and 2 FT + 4 C. These cost totals include more than the published monthly overhead range; reconcile deal costs, contractors, servicing, and credit losses separately.

Protect fees by documenting what is earned, when it is earned, and which authorized account pays it. A buyer's down payment can be consideration toward property acquisition or principal, rather than a standalone fee. An option payment can carry refund, credit, or performance conditions. Have the accountant map each component to the applicable accounting guidance and avoid treating every dollar arriving at closing as current income. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis can matter for qualifying service arrangements; mortgage interest and financial assets require their own accounting treatment. For this scorecard, the retained operator basis excludes underlying property value, pass-through debt service, and customer escrow. Do not deduct underlying interest twice after already calculating retained interest revenue. Contracts should state the consideration, funding source, permitted setoffs, cancellation treatment, and disbursement instructions. Record security instruments through the settlement process, retain executed note custody records, and document any later assignment. Those protections preserve enforceable rights; they do not authorize self-help eviction, unilateral account withdrawals, or fee extraction from protected funds. If a buyer disputes an ancillary charge, isolate the dispute while continuing accurate allocation of undisputed mortgage payments under the governing documents and law.

sections.heading: 4. Screen statutory exposure and build a funded fallback before collecting
paragraphs: Make licensed origination the operating standard for every owner-occupant wrap buyer in this playbook. The SAFE Act framework, including 12 U.S.C. §5103, governs licensing or registration for covered loan originators. Dodd-Frank's residential mortgage provisions and Regulation Z impose additional obligations when their coverage tests apply. The ability-to-repay rule in 12 CFR §1026.43 requires a reasonable, good-faith repayment determination for covered transactions. Limited seller-financer exclusions within 12 CFR §1026.36 do not create a universal exemption from every lending, disclosure, or state requirement. Give the RMLO the actual note terms, balloon provisions, fees, property charges, and borrower documents rather than asking them to approve a predetermined payment. In Texas, review Finance Code Chapter 159 for residential wrap mortgage origination requirements and Property Code §5.016 for applicable encumbered-property conveyance notices. These provisions address different duties, and exceptions must be checked against the actual facts. Do not collapse them into a generic signed acknowledgment. Establish the required notice recipients, delivery methods, timing, licensing status, and evidence retention before scheduling closing. A settlement date chosen for marketing convenience cannot shorten a statutory notice period.

The mapped play distressed_asset_recovery, Distressed Asset Recovery — TRACK_1, offers an adjacent sourcing and revenue discipline: locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets and earn a lawful recovery fee or acquisition spread. Its universe includes tax-sale overages, state unclaimed funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, and distressed micro-businesses; each asset type has different ownership and collection rules. A homeowner's surplus claim is not automatically collateral for your wrap transaction. Suppose a separate verified claim produces $30,000, and the applicable jurisdiction permits a properly documented 10% contingent recovery fee. The fee is $3,000, the claimant receives $27,000 before any separately authorized charges, and $800 of direct research and permitted filing support leaves $2,200 before overhead. If a statutory cap or waiting period prevents that contract, revise the structure or decline; do not relabel the fee. Screen assignments, heirship, competing liens, foreclosure distribution priorities, and representation restrictions before forecasting collection. The prescribed fallback is diversification across multi-state dockets with attorney-backed filing partnerships where required. That means jurisdiction-specific procedures and qualified local professionals, not shopping for weaker consumer protections. Keep this separate example outside the canonical wrap revenue bridge unless explicitly budgeted.

Design the failure response while everyone is still cooperative. If the underlying lender accelerates, immediately obtain the written demand and a verified payoff figure, involve transaction counsel, and evaluate funded refinancing, negotiated resolution, or an orderly sale. A $180,000 principal balance can require more than $180,000 to resolve after accrued interest and permitted costs; a $2,700 installment reserve is plainly not an acceleration reserve. Never conceal ownership changes or make false occupancy statements to preserve a rate. If the buyer defaults, continue underlying payments from operator liquidity while the servicer applies notices, loss-mitigation procedures, and foreclosure requirements applicable to that account. Regulation X provisions such as 12 CFR §1024.41 have defined coverage and exemptions; have the servicer document applicability instead of assuming every portfolio follows identical procedures. Budget a six-month $900 installment interruption as $5,400 before property protection, counsel, taxes, and insurance. Review reserve adequacy monthly against actual delinquencies and renewal costs. Payment monitoring must prove receipt by the underlying lender, not merely a debit from your servicer. Withhold owner distributions when reconciliation breaks, then restore them only after the shortage and its cause are resolved.

callout.title: Four verifications before funds become distributable
callout.body: A signed contract and a visible bank balance are insufficient. Assign an accountable reviewer to each verification and retain the evidence in the transaction record.
items: Confirm title, execution authority, bankruptcy status, underlying loan terms, and a funded response to acceleration before acquiring the property.
Confirm licensed RMLO underwriting, applicable disclosures, state wrap requirements, and an affordable fully loaded payment before financing the buyer.
Confirm licensed servicing, segregated escrow responsibilities, independently verified settlement instructions, and a successful boarding reconciliation before collecting scheduled installments.
Confirm underlying lender receipt, current tax and insurance funding, resolved payment exceptions, and adequate operator reserves before releasing owner distributions.

chapters.pull_quote: A wrap spread belongs to the operator only after every underlying obligation is paid, every protected balance is intact, and the ledger proves the difference.
action_checklist: Create a party-and-authority register covering record owners, buyers, lenders, settlement professionals, the licensed RMLO, and the licensed servicer.
Build a property-specific due-on-sale exposure memo with a verified payoff estimate and a credible funding or sale response.
Obtain documented owner-occupant repayment underwriting and complete applicable federal and state notices before scheduling closing.
Approve an eight-rail payment policy distinguishing funds-transfer methods from escrow controls, retainers, statutory distributions, and milestone holds.
Reconcile each borrower collection to principal, retained interest, underlying remittance, servicing expense, and protected tax and insurance balances.
Reproduce the $28,000, $190,000, and $442,000 profit cases without counting property value, debt principal, customer escrow, or unbudgeted recovery fees as wrap revenue.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #35, Subject-To & Wraparound Note Arbitrage, ranks #09 of 36 with a Money-to-Manpower Score of 90/100 and 11 mapped plays. Its economic engine is retained upfront spread plus performing wrap interest margin, never property value or borrowed principal. This chapter reconciles the Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual owner profits of $28,000, $190,000, and $442,000 through explicit acquisition, labor, servicing, origination, carrying, and reversal deductions. It connects probate-docket sourcing to measured acquisition cost, distinguishes collection delays from contractual payment timing, and sizes liquidity independently of reported profit. Licensed RMLO underwriting, licensed third-party servicing, verified underlying payments, and state-specific transfer procedures determine whether attractive paper spreads survive actual operations.

sections.heading: 1. Normalize buyer collections into earned, retained cohort economics
paragraphs: Start with a collection ledger, not the purchase price printed on a deed. The canonical scorecard reports $100,000, $475,000, and $850,000 of annual operator revenue on a retained-spread basis. For a transparent reconciliation, model four, fifteen, and twenty-five new closings with earned upfront spreads of $15,000, $20,000, and $22,000 each. Those closings contribute $60,000, $300,000, and $550,000. Separately, eight, thirty-five, and sixty performing note-year equivalents contribute $5,000 each, producing $40,000, $175,000, and $300,000. A note-year equivalent means twelve months of performing exposure; two notes performing for six months equal one equivalent. These are mixed-vintage portfolio illustrations, not claims that this year's closings instantly create an entire seasoned book. Document beginning balances, acquisition dates, payoffs, and delinquency periods before assigning exposure. The resulting totals reconcile exactly to the three scorecard cases without counting home values, borrowed principal, or pass-through payments as revenue. Maintain one property identifier across title records, the wrap note, underlying loan statements, and servicing exports. Without that join, a payoff or duplicate receipt can make an apparently excellent cohort profitable twice while its actual cash reserve remains empty. Track seasoning explicitly in every monthly performance review.

The cash bridge assumes buyer closing collections of $25,000, $30,000, and $32,000 per new transaction, with $10,000 per closing assigned to principal, restricted amounts, or documented reimbursements rather than operator income. The remaining illustrative spreads require actual earned economics and supporting agreements; a down payment alone does not establish revenue. Across the portfolios, gross closing collections therefore equal $100,000, $450,000, and $800,000. Illustrative annual wrap interest receipts are $10,500 per performing note-year, against $5,500 of underlying interest, leaving the modeled $5,000 margin. Combined collections in this limited bridge are $184,000, $817,500, and $1,430,000. Remove $40,000, $150,000, and $250,000 of excluded closing cash, then $44,000, $192,500, and $330,000 of underlying interest to recover the canonical totals. Principal amortization and escrow collections sit outside this bridge and still require separate cash schedules. The interest amounts are annual exposure assumptions, not a recommended interest-only consumer product or an amortization quote. For actual notes, calculate interest from outstanding balances and payment dates, then replace the simplifying assumptions without changing the revenue definition or disguising principal as yield.

Keep the management scorecard separate from financial-statement recognition. Calling retained spread gross revenue in the supplied model does not make all customer receipts revenue under generally accepted accounting principles. ASC 606 principal-agent analysis can govern qualifying service arrangements, while note interest, loan accounting, and property dispositions require their applicable accounting guidance. Do not automatically apply a single retained_share percentage to a property sale or offset legally distinct interest accounts in the statutory books. An accountant should map each transaction to its actual contract, asset, obligation, and recognition timing, with a reconciliation back to this operator dashboard. Likewise, a refundable option deposit remains a liability until its contractual treatment supports recognition. Show restricted escrow, refundable deposits, principal collections, earned fees, and interest margin as separate ledger categories in QuickBooks or an equivalent accounting system. Export the licensed servicer's payment allocation report and reconcile it against bank settlement, not merely the borrower's payment confirmation. A collection that later reverses must reverse the relevant receivable or revenue treatment without deleting the event history. This discipline makes the annual margin waterfall auditable and prevents cash temporarily held for another party from financing owner distributions.

sections.heading: 2. Charge every acquisition, contractor hour, and reversal to the waterfall
paragraphs: Use eight expense pools and prohibit double booking between them. Annual acquisition cost is $12,000, $45,000, and $65,000, equivalent to $3,000, $3,000, and $2,600 per new closing. Delivery labor consumes $18,000, $75,000, and $108,000, covering hired transaction coordination, underwriting support, document collection, and operational staff time. Servicing and payment-audit expense adds $6,000, $24,000, and $42,000. Legal, title, and licensed RMLO work costs $8,000, $30,000, and $42,000; borrower-paid charges reimbursing these costs must receive consistent ledger treatment. Carrying and workout expense contributes $8,000, $36,000, and $54,000. Scrub and reversal provisioning adds $6,000, $25,000, and $35,000. Fixed operating overhead contributes $14,000, $50,000, and $62,000. These seven deductions total $72,000, $285,000, and $408,000; the eighth pool is the resulting owner-profit residual. That residual is $28,000, $190,000, and $442,000, exactly 28%, 40.0%, and 52% of canonical revenue. Owner compensation comes from this residual; do not describe it as profit after an additional founder salary. Team capacity remains one full-time operator plus three contractors in the first two cases, and two full-time operators plus four contractors when scaled.

Unpack probate_docket_inheritance_arbitrage as a measured sourcing channel, not an assumed right to collect transaction commissions. This is the specified play within the volume's eleven mapped plays. Parse county probate petitions, Letters Testamentary, Letters of Administration, and daily Notice-of-Default filings through permitted public-record access. Match parcel identifiers, representative addresses, filing dates, and case status before routing records to licensed probate brokers or cash buyers. An illustrative Base acquisition budget funds 1,500 deduplicated records at $12 each, or $18,000, plus $27,000 of verification, outreach, and broker coordination. If fifteen eligible closings result, $45,000 divided by fifteen produces the modeled $3,000 acquisition cost. A one-percent closing yield is an assumption requiring cohort evidence, not a county-record conversion promise. Confirm the representative's current authority and any required court permission before negotiating with an estate. Where transaction-linked compensation requires licensure, use a licensed brokerage of record or switch to genuine flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions. Six licensed-agent subscribers paying $250 monthly generate $18,000 annually, enough to cover the illustrated record cost but not the entire acquisition program. Treat that fallback as separate service economics, never extra scorecard revenue.

The reversal pool must distinguish rejected leads, failed closings, returned payments, contractual refunds, and credit losses. Acquisition scrubs already absorbed in the $45,000 Base sourcing budget cannot also consume the $25,000 reversal provision. Instead, build that Base provision from $10,000 of post-recognition refund exposure, $5,000 of collection reversals, and $10,000 of incremental loss exposure not included in carrying costs. These allocations illustrate budgeting, while booked allowances follow the applicable accounting treatment and actual evidence. Carrying expense covers cash costs such as vacancy, preservation, and workout administration; loss provisioning captures distinct expected economic impairments. Track contractor labor by file and outcome, including abandoned files, rather than charging only successful closings. A hypothetical $75,000 Base labor budget supports 1,500 purchased hours at a blended $50 hourly cost. Dividing by fifteen closings yields 100 hours per funded outcome, including failed-file work. If the queue consumes 1,800 hours, the $15,000 overrun reduces Base profit to $175,000 before any other change. Review actual work allocation with the full-time operator; software can reconcile payments and flag exceptions, but it cannot erase unresolved title defects or substitute for licensed underwriting judgment.

callout.title: Price the files that never close
callout.body: Cohort profitability improves when failed-file costs remain visible and retained cash is distinguished from money merely passing through.
items: Attach every county-record invoice to its acquisition month; calculate cost per eligible closing only after that cohort seasons.
Request the licensed servicer's transaction-level allocation export, then match underlying lender posting dates rather than relying on a payment-sent status.
Price estate-authority verification before buyer underwriting; discovering defective representative authority after paid RMLO work compounds abandoned-file expense.
Keep subscription contracts independent of transaction success; do not disguise referral compensation as a data invoice or add fallback receipts to the canonical cases.

sections.heading: 3. Fund collection lag, locked payouts, and underlying-payment continuity separately
paragraphs: Profit is a period measure; liquidity is a dated obligation schedule. For recurring charges, calculate days sales outstanding from earned receivables and their actual collection dates. Do not call the entire property principal balance overdue revenue. For acquisitions, separately measure days from the first unreimbursed expenditure to unrestricted closing proceeds. This illustration uses effective funding lags of forty-five, sixty, and seventy-five days, with committed monthly operating burn of $2,000, $6,000, and $12,000. Those assumptions require $3,000, $12,000, and $30,000 of operating-lag liquidity using thirty-day months. The burn amounts are subsets of the annual expense waterfall, not additional deductions, and distinguish fixed commitments from variable deal spending. They sit within the supplied monthly operating range without claiming that total annual expenses are limited to twelve times that range. Contractor invoices, closing costs, and workout events remain incremental cash events on the schedule. Use a thirteen-week forecast with exact tax, insurance, underlying mortgage, contractor, and servicer dates. A positive month-end balance can conceal a midmonth shortfall when the underlying payment falls due before buyer funds settle. Test daily minimum cash, not just monthly totals.

Add payout-lock exposure explicitly rather than hiding it inside average collection timing. Assume ten percent of earned upfront spread remains unavailable on one, two, and three concurrent closings. That creates $1,500, $4,000, and $6,600 of additional locked cash. This is a stress assumption, not a universal servicer policy; replace it with the settlement agreement, return exposure, and documented release dates. Next reserve three months of the simplified underlying interest obligation: $11,000, $48,125, and $82,500 across the modeled portfolios. Actual amortizing loan payments require additional principal liquidity. Add three months of a $300 monthly tax-and-insurance obligation per performing exposure unit, yielding $7,200, $31,500, and $54,000. This is operator backup capital for collection failure, separate from borrower escrow held for its designated purpose. Actual reserve sizing uses current active loans rather than annual equivalents; the illustration assumes those counts coincide at the measurement date. Neither tax reserves nor escrow accounts can fund acquisition marketing. Maintain account-level cash restrictions, and confirm insurance coverage fits the actual ownership and occupancy arrangement. A paid premium does not prove the policy correctly covers the transferred risk.

Finally, cash-fund the annual reversal allowance of $6,000, $25,000, and $35,000 and stage incremental deal expenditure outside committed operating burn. Assume $9,500, $10,000, and $8,600 of acquisition, variable delivery, and closing outlay per simultaneous file, with one, two, and three files prefunded. These timing assumptions create $9,500, $20,000, and $25,800 of deal float; validate that invoices included here are excluded from the fixed-burn calculation. Combined illustrative liquidity is $38,200, $140,625, and $233,900. Funding reserves moves cash into protected availability; it does not create a second expense after the provision already reduced profit. The supplied $12,000-$65,000 startup range can support a narrowly staged launch, but it does not finance the entire Base or Scaled reserve stack. Bridge that difference with accumulated retained earnings, fewer concurrent files, or committed financing whose covenants permit the use. Do not rely on the next buyer's refundable deposit. None of these totals funds full due-on-sale acceleration, acquisition equity, or a major rehabilitation. Model those exposures separately using actual payoff balances and executable financing or sale alternatives before accepting a transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Stress retained margin before committing capital to a transfer
paragraphs: Run sensitivities against the canonical cases without silently rebuilding their expense assumptions. A twenty-percent reduction in retained revenue, with all modeled expenses held constant, leaves $8,000, $95,000, and $272,000 of owner profit. A fifty-percent acquisition-cost increase alone leaves $22,000, $167,500, and $409,500. A twenty-percent reduction in retained annual interest margin alone removes $8,000, $35,000, and $60,000, leaving $20,000, $155,000, and $382,000. Doubling the reversal provision alone leaves $22,000, $165,000, and $407,000. Combine the revenue reduction, acquisition inflation, and doubled reversal provision, but do not also subtract the interest-only sensitivity because that would overlap the revenue shock. Combined profit becomes a $4,000 loss, $47,500 profit, and $204,500 profit. These are deterministic tests, not probability-weighted forecasts. Their purpose is to expose how the Conservative case fails before larger portfolios exhaust their apparent margin. Record which expenses truly flex with volume and which remain contractual commitments. A contractor cancellation right may reduce future spending, but it does not cancel work already performed or restore a refund already paid. Reforecast cash and earnings together after each observed variance.

A profitable stress case can still fail through acceleration or an unworkable foreclosure timeline. The Garn-St Germain framework at 12 U.S.C. 1701j-3 permits enforcement of due-on-sale clauses subject to specified limits and exceptions; an ordinary investor subject-to purchase is not automatically protected. Neither a wrap note nor timely payments remove the underlying lender's contractual rights. Obtain written lender consent where required for the chosen structure, or price the acceleration exposure with an executable alternative rather than a hoped-for refinance. Underwrite each owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO, document the applicable ability-to-repay analysis under 12 CFR 1026.43, and determine licensing and seller-financer treatment under the actual facts. The SAFE Act and Regulation Z contain distinct requirements; using an RMLO does not automatically satisfy every creditor duty. For Texas transactions, evaluate Property Code Section 5.016 notice requirements and Finance Code Chapter 159 wrap-mortgage requirements, including their applicability and exceptions. Budget required notices, disclosures, delivery evidence, and timing before scheduling settlement. If the structure cannot satisfy applicable requirements economically, decline the acquisition or route it through a properly structured conventional sale.

Make the final investment decision with three separate outputs: recognized operator economics, unrestricted liquidity, and maximum event exposure. For the Base case, the starting outputs are $190,000 annual owner profit, $140,625 illustrative operating liquidity, and an additional acceleration exposure determined from actual underlying payoff statements. The first two numbers cannot substitute for the third. Require the licensed servicer to report delinquency aging, underlying-payment confirmation, escrow sufficiency, and unresolved exceptions each month. Validate licensing for the relevant state and activity rather than assuming a national software brand supplies the required authorization. Set distribution policy around verified unrestricted cash after reserve restoration, not a percentage of buyer receipts. When a buyer defaults, preserve records, obtain the jurisdiction-specific enforcement timeline, and forecast taxes, insurance, property protection, and debt payments through resolution. Do not assume immediate possession or immediate resale. Feed actual recoveries and timing back into cohort assumptions quarterly. Keep the eleven-play portfolio narrative subordinate to the verified file-level economics: an early probate record is useful only when authority, title, buyer capacity, servicing, and cash continuity all support a transaction that the operator can fund through a bad outcome.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you allocate startup capital ($12,000–$65,000 USD) and configure a lean, low-opex ($2,000–$12,000 USD/mo) production stack without wasting cash on bloated overhead?
chapters.title: Startup Capital, Lean Infrastructure & Pre-Flight Stack
chapters.subtitle: Reserve-First Capital, RMLO Underwriting, Licensed Servicing, Garn-St Germain Exposure & Twelve Lean Operating Layers
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #35, Subject-To & Wraparound Note Arbitrage, ranks #09 of 36 with a 90/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Across the volume's 11 mapped plays, capital discipline matters more than software breadth: protect at least half of startup cash, buy transaction-specific expertise, and verify every underlying payment. Canonical annual owner profits are $28,000 Conservative, $190,000 Base, and $442,000 Scaled, measured against operator spread revenue rather than property values or mortgage principal. This chapter allocates $12,000–$65,000, specifies twelve infrastructure layers, separates fixed overhead from transaction costs, and establishes evidence-based launch requirements. HOA priority and tax-redemption opportunities receive their own rights analysis and loss limits, never automatic access to mortgage-payment reserves.

sections.heading: 1. Protect the reserve before buying a single acquisition channel
paragraphs: Start with liquidity, not a purchase contract. At $12,000, ring-fence $6,500, or 54.2%, as working-capital and payment float; at $65,000, protect $35,000, or 53.8%. The remaining allocations in the capital matrix sum exactly to $5,500 and $30,000. These are spending ceilings, not instructions to empty each envelope before closing. Obtain transaction-specific quotes from local real-estate counsel, a licensed residential mortgage loan originator, title personnel, and the proposed servicer before committing acquisition cash. Keep reserve money in a separately identified operating savings account, not mixed with buyer escrow or security deposits. At the $2,000 monthly overhead floor, $6,500 buys only 3.25 months before property carrying costs. Because first-deal timing is two to six months, the minimum startup budget cannot fund six months of full overhead plus a troubled property. Begin with staged diligence and minimal subscriptions, maintain documented outside runway, or postpone acquisition. A smaller budget changes the permitted transaction, not the required reserve. Review bank balances weekly against committed invoices, upcoming debt-service dates, insurance premiums, and any earnest-money exposure that could become nonrefundable. Exclude hoped-for buyer deposits from available liquidity until receipt, contractual treatment, and disbursement authority are established.

Treat monthly overhead and portfolio economics as separate ledgers. The canonical Conservative case produces $100,000 of operator revenue and $28,000 of owner profit, leaving $72,000 of total annual expense. An illustrative $2,000 monthly fixed stack consumes $24,000, leaving $48,000 for transaction expenses, contractors, servicing, losses, and other modeled costs. Base revenue of $475,000 less $190,000 profit leaves $285,000; allocating $6,000 monthly to fixed overhead leaves $213,000 for other annual expenses. Scaled revenue of $850,000 less $442,000 profit leaves $408,000; $12,000 monthly fixed overhead leaves $264,000. These allocations reconcile the supplied scenarios without claiming the scorecard prescribes those individual expense buckets. Reserve transfers are balance-sheet movements, not another expense deduction. Contractor counts describe capacity relationships, not four full-time salaries hidden inside a tiny software budget. The Conservative and Base teams remain one full-time operator plus three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time operators plus four contractors. Add recurring staff only after realized collections support the increase through a stressed quarter. Do not extrapolate annual profit from one unusually large closing spread or treat the headline margin as a monthly cash-distribution instruction. Build the cash forecast around actual due dates and collectible receipts.

Size deal float from obligations rather than purchase price. For illustration, a $200,000 underlying balance amortized over thirty years at 3% requires approximately $843.21 monthly principal and interest. Add $350 for property taxes and insurance, $35 servicing, and a $200 maintenance allowance: the planning burden becomes $1,428.21 monthly. Six months requires $8,569.26 before foreclosure counsel, HOA assessments, vacancy repairs, or acceleration exposure. The $6,500 minimum-budget reserve therefore cannot support this example without additional dedicated liquidity. Tax and insurance obligations remain payable even when the wrap buyer stops paying; collecting escrow does not eliminate the need to reconcile it. Keep a property-level reserve schedule showing obligation, due date, responsible payer, and source statement. Never solve a shortage by borrowing another borrower's escrow or spending a refundable deposit. For an underlying lender's acceleration demand, six months of installments is not a cure fund: document a separately credible refinance, sale, or negotiated resolution path. Reject a transaction when the exit requires appreciation, an unqualified replacement borrower, or concealment of the transfer. Cash preservation means declining otherwise attractive spreads when the downside exceeds the funded operating envelope.
