callout.title: Protect the payment machine before expanding acquisition
callout.body: Experienced operators buy evidence and execution capacity before they buy a larger lead funnel.
items: Obtain an underlying-payment history before pricing the spread; delinquency cures consume cash that the advertised mortgage rate conceals.
Schedule servicer remittance ahead of the underlying due date, allowing for the provider's documented ACH settlement and return windows.
Keep payment float separate from acquisition cash, with a property-level subledger proving that each committed obligation remains funded.
Negotiate fixed-scope counsel and RMLO engagements; a cheap document template cannot resolve a state-specific licensing or lien-priority defect.

sections.heading: 2. Assemble twelve operating layers without twelve expensive subscriptions
paragraphs: The infrastructure matrix specifies twelve functions, not twelve mandatory paid subscriptions. Its exact dollar amounts are planning inputs using named public-plan examples, not verified current offers; confirm checkout prices, geographic availability, taxes, billing cadence, and feature limits before purchase. Quote-based services receive explicit internal allowances rather than invented vendor tariffs. One operator can begin with Google Workspace Business Starter at an assumed $7 monthly annual-commitment rate, Bitwarden Teams at an assumed $4 monthly annual-billing rate, and QuickBooks Online Simple Start at an assumed $38 monthly standard rate. Those three inputs total $49 monthly before tax, domain registration, and professional services. Free HubSpot, Trello, Calendly, and Adobe Acrobat Reader tiers cover basic pipeline, tasks, booking, and document inspection. Do not count an unused subscription as production capacity. A licensed servicer and RMLO are external operating relationships with onboarding, document, and per-file charges; their costs belong in deal underwriting. The $2,000 monthly opex floor must also absorb actual administrative support, insurance, outreach, accounting assistance, and telephone costs. Software alone neither explains that floor nor justifies spending up to it. Start billing only when a named person owns the function.

Configure one property identifier across CRM, document storage, accounting, servicing, and the reserve register. Use a consistent record such as ST035-0001 rather than borrower Social Security numbers in filenames or email subjects. HubSpot should hold lead source, property address, seller contact permission, next action, and stage; the RMLO's approved portal should hold income evidence and sensitive application material. Google Drive folders need named-user access, multifactor authentication, restricted sharing, and a documented retention schedule. Bitwarden stores credentials and recovery procedures, not a shared password copied into Trello. Give contractors only the records required for their assignments, remove access at engagement end, and keep an access register. Underlying lender access must follow the lender's authorization process; never impersonate the original borrower. Send third-party providers only the information their work requires through approved channels. Export the pipeline and accounting records regularly, then test whether a replacement operator can locate the executed note, recorded security instrument, insurance evidence, payment history, and next maturity date. A backup becomes useful only when restoration and document completeness have been demonstrated. Assign a second authorized person to emergency payment continuity.

Automate exception detection before automating deal selection. A low-equity or foreclosure-status trigger should create a research task, not an automatic offer or bulk message. Verify public-record dates, reinstatement amounts, contact restrictions, and whether a seller is represented. The servicer should supply a monthly borrower ledger, remittance detail, escrow activity, and exception report, while the operator independently verifies the underlying mortgage payment and insurance status. Autopay enrollment does not prove settlement; returned ACH entries and unapplied funds need assigned owners. Start with read-only exports and calendar reminders. Add integrations only after matching record identifiers, testing duplicate handling, and defining who resolves missing data. Budget a $35 per-note monthly servicing allowance for comparison, but replace it with the provider's written schedule covering setup, late payments, escrow administration, statements, payoff requests, and transfers. Five notes at that allowance cost $175 monthly before extras. Do not select a servicer solely because the headline charge is lower: confirm required licenses, funds segregation, reporting capability, complaint handling, and support for the proposed wrap structure. Vendor branding is not evidence of authorization in the property's jurisdiction. Retain a documented migration procedure before onboarding the first account.

sections.heading: 3. Separate legal ownership, recognized spreads, and statutory sidecar risk
paragraphs: Choose the entity and banking structure with counsel and the tax preparer before taking title. An LLC filing does not authorize mortgage origination, servicing, brokerage, or escrow custody. Obtain an EIN, adopt signing authority, document beneficial ownership for bank onboarding, and maintain books that distinguish each property and obligation. The underlying borrower remains liable unless the lender expressly releases them; taking title subject to a mortgage does not create that release. Under 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3, due-on-sale enforcement and specific statutory exceptions require transaction-level review. A trust or entity wrapper does not manufacture an exception for an otherwise covered sale. Disclose the structure accurately to the insurer and obtain appropriate named-insured, mortgagee, occupancy, and loss-payee treatment. Confirm vacancy, rental, seller-financing, and liability exposures rather than assuming the seller's old policy survives unchanged. Require an insurable-interest review and evidence of coverage effective at transfer. Maintain separate authorizations for lender communication and servicer instructions. Bank account labels do not transform operator-controlled funds into a lawful escrow arrangement; use the authorized custodian where required. Reconcile custodial balances separately from operating cash and prohibit owner distributions from funds owed to borrowers or underlying creditors.

Build the revenue ledger around the supplied economic basis: net upfront option or down-payment spreads and retained annual wrap interest margin, excluding house value and pass-through debt service. Consider an illustrative $240,000 resale with $20,000 down and a $220,000 wrap amortized over thirty years at 7%. Its monthly payment is approximately $1,463.67. Against the earlier $843.21 underlying payment, the cash difference is $620.46, or $585.46 after a $35 servicing allowance, before other costs. First-month wrap interest is $1,283.33 and underlying interest is $500; the $783.33 interest difference is not the same as the cash-payment difference because principal amortization differs. Likewise, $20,000 down less $8,000 seller consideration, $4,000 closing cash, and $6,000 retained liquidity leaves $2,000 freely deployable cash, not automatically $2,000 recognized profit. Have the accountant apply the relevant real-estate and financial-instrument guidance; ASC 606 principal-agent analysis applies where within scope, not indiscriminately to loan interest. The supplied scorecard contains no separate retained-share multiplier, so do not apply a second haircut to its canonical operator-revenue totals. Reconcile cash, earned spreads, principal, escrow, and deferred amounts through distinct ledger accounts.

Ring-fence hoa_super_lien_tax_deed_redemption_arbitrage as a separate TRACK_1 rights strategy, never a shortcut to free-and-clear title. For a counsel-cleared HOA claim, suppose enforceable priority components total $2,400, the interest costs $1,600, and a documented collectible payoff is $2,700. After $300 collection expense and $64 carrying cost at 12% annually for four months, the illustrative contribution is $736. The payoff assumption needs an itemized legal basis; lien face value does not establish priority, collectibility, or a statutory yield. Tax-sale redemption is a different instrument. Under Texas Tax Code §34.21, property category, redemption timing, permitted expenditures, and tender mechanics determine the calculation. An eligible first-year redemption with a $10,000 statutory base and applicable 25% premium produces $12,500; subtracting the $10,000 investment, $1,000 diligence expense, and $500 carrying cost leaves $1,000. That result requires actual qualifying redemption, not merely winning an auction. Do not fund this $10,000 position from the minimum launch reserve. On defective notice, disputed priority, or uncertain redemption rights, suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests. Never treat the mortgage as extinguished without transaction-specific authority and title analysis.

sections.heading: 4. Run the pre-launch rehearsal before accepting borrower money
paragraphs: Before launch, have counsel map the proposed seller-financing activity to federal and state requirements, then route every owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO as the operating standard. The SAFE Act framework in 12 U.S.C. §§5101–5116, Regulation Z loan-originator provisions in 12 CFR §1026.36, and ability-to-repay requirements in 12 CFR §1026.43 have scope conditions and exclusions that must be evaluated rather than flattened into a universal exemption. Collect verified income, obligations, credit information, and the applicable payment calculation through the originator's process. Do not advertise a borrower as qualified because their down payment covers the acquisition advance. For Texas transactions, review Property Code §5.016 notices for covered encumbered-property conveyances and Finance Code Chapter 159 requirements for wrap mortgage lending, including applicable licensing, disclosures, and closing procedures. A notice is not lender permission and does not erase acceleration exposure. Create a transaction-specific evidence index showing who prepared each document, who reviewed it, when delivery occurred, and where receipt evidence resides. Stop the file when required borrower qualification or notice evidence is missing, even if the seller offers a closing discount. Speed cannot repair an unenforceable instrument.

Rehearse one complete payment cycle using test records before taking live collections. Enter the buyer amount due, expected receipt date, servicing charge, underlying installment, escrow allocation, and reserve contribution. Model an ACH return after a provisional posting, a tax bill increase, an insurance cancellation notice, and an underlying payment credited to suspense rather than the scheduled installment. Each exception needs an owner, deadline, escalation route, and documentary resolution. The servicer's statement should reconcile to bank activity, while the underlying creditor's statement independently confirms application. Require dual review of new payout destinations and verify wire changes through a trusted telephone number already on file. Keep emergency payment authority separate from authority to change bank details. Document how the backup operator acts if the founder is unavailable on the mortgage due date. For insurance and tax administration, record renewal dates and reconcile actual disbursements rather than relying on dashboard status. Test exporting the complete loan history before accepting a servicing contract. A migration plan needs usable documents, balances, transaction history, and custodial reconciliation, not merely a promise that another provider can take over. Record rehearsal defects and resolve them before live payment instructions are issued.

Release acquisition spending in stages tied to evidence. First authorize limited records research; next authorize title and counsel review; then authorize borrower underwriting and final document preparation. Preserve contractual diligence exits where available and calendar the exact date money becomes exposed. Before closing, produce a one-page cash bridge showing starting unrestricted cash, closing outflows, remaining reserve, next ninety days of obligations, and a six-month buyer-default case. Reconcile it to bank evidence and provider quotes, not CRM estimates. The founder signs the operating decision after the relevant professionals complete their assigned work; no software status substitutes for their findings. After closing, audit the first three payment cycles individually before increasing volume. Compare actual servicing fees, cure costs, collection timing, and retained interest against the acquisition model. Expand only when funded float grows with the obligations and exception work remains manageable by the stated team. Keep HOA and tax-redemption positions outside the wrap portfolio's payment reserve and report their realized results separately. If acquisition economics weaken, cut lead spending first, preserve servicing and evidence collection, and decline new obligations until liquidity recovers. The cheapest production stack is the one that avoids financing preventable operating mistakes.

sections.heading: 1. Kill the Deal Before a Senior Lien Kills the Spread
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is treating a subject-to deed as a lender-approved assumption. Title can transfer while the seller remains personally liable on the existing note; neither a servicing agreement nor punctual payments automatically removes the lender's contractual acceleration rights. Read the note, security instrument, riders, modification history, and any assumption provisions before quoting a spread. Under 12 U.S.C. § 1701j-3, certain transfers receive statutory protection, but an ordinary investor purchase does not become protected merely because someone inserts a trust. The inter vivos trust exception has specific borrower-beneficiary and occupancy-right conditions. Never manufacture occupancy statements or hide a transfer through misleading correspondence. Obtain written lender consent or model acceleration as a live exposure. For an illustrative $180,000 senior balance, $15,000 of cash cannot fund payoff; even a refinance requires executable credit, valuation, timing, and closing proceeds. Maintain an independent sale alternative and a current payoff estimate. Stop acquisition when neither consent nor a credible payoff path exists within the proposed risk budget. A low coupon is valuable only while the capital structure survives the lender exercising its rights. Document who receives lender notices and how the seller forwards them immediately, without surrendering access to their own account.

The second trap is buying an attractive payment instead of a verified lien stack. Obtain a title commitment, recorded instruments, current senior statement, authorized payoff information, tax status, association balances, and pending foreclosure docket entries. A reinstatement quote does not establish a full payoff, and an online balance may omit recoverable advances, default interest, trustee charges, or a deferred modification balance. Ask the title agent to identify junior liens, judgments, vesting defects, marital interests, and exceptions that remain after closing. For a $220,000 property with $180,000 senior debt, an undiscovered $18,000 junior lien consumes nearly half the apparent $40,000 equity before selling expenses. An $8,000 tax lien and $12,000 disposition budget eliminate the rest. Do not describe that exposure as a documentation inconvenience. Require an updated search through recording, documented releases where needed, and explicit allocation of cure costs. Fraudulent notarization, forged seller authority, or an unsupported power of attorney requires stopping the transaction, not adding a price discount. The fallback is a properly cured closing or withdrawal. Maintain evidence of seller identity and voluntary execution through the closing professional, with access restricted to people actually performing the transaction.

The third and fourth traps are buying a foreclosure clock and leaving insurance written for yesterday's ownership. Public notices can identify distress, but they do not establish sufficient time to cure, transfer title, underwrite a buyer, or record documents. Have local foreclosure counsel map the actual sale date, postponement evidence, reinstatement deadline, and any bankruptcy stay under 11 U.S.C. § 362. Do not assume a seller's verbal account of postponement changes the docket. Separately, have the insurance producer confirm the correct insured interests, occupancy, vacancy conditions, mortgagee provisions, deductibles, and effective dates. A seller's old homeowner policy is not an operating plan for an investor-owned property occupied by a wrap buyer. Bind appropriate coverage without misrepresenting ownership. Budget taxes and insurance from current assessments and replacement-cost quotations, not last year's escrow installment. If monthly escrow rises from $350 to $525, the additional $175 consumes 35% of a $500 monthly spread before servicing. Require a reserve replenishment plan before releasing distributions. The circuit-breaker is immediate review of any cancellation, force-placed coverage notice, tax delinquency, or unverified sale postponement; those events outrank a new acquisition and receive a named owner on the same business day.

sections.heading: 2. Originate a Collectible Note Instead of a Refund Obligation
paragraphs: The fifth trap is assuming seller financing sits outside mortgage origination rules. For every owner-occupant wrap buyer, this operating model uses a properly licensed residential mortgage loan originator and a documented ability-to-repay assessment. Verify the individual and sponsoring entity through NMLS Consumer Access, then verify authority for the property state and proposed activity. The SAFE Act framework in 12 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116 and state implementation govern licensing; Regulation Z separately addresses loan-originator rules, covered-creditor duties, and repayment analysis. Seller-financer exclusions under 12 CFR § 1026.36(a)(4) and (5) have distinct conditions and do not erase every other obligation. Require counsel and the RMLO to classify creditor status, transaction coverage, disclosures, high-cost features, and applicable state restrictions before choosing terms. Underwrite income, assets relied upon, existing obligations, housing costs, and payment changes using reliable records where required. A buyer earning $5,000 monthly with $2,200 housing expense and $900 other debt has a 62% illustrative debt-to-income ratio; a large deposit does not cure unaffordable payments. Reject fabricated income, coached omissions, and undocumented exceptions. The fallback is a supportable structure or no loan, never a stronger collection script.

The sixth trap is confusing signed disclosure pages with an enforceable closing process. In Texas, examine both Tex. Prop. Code § 5.016 and the wrap mortgage framework in Tex. Fin. Code Chapter 159; their applicability, exceptions, notices, timing, licensing, and remedies require separate analysis. Section 5.016 addresses covered conveyances subject to recorded liens and includes advance notice requirements; do not reduce the analysis to a buyer initialing a form at the signing table. Chapter 159 adds wrap-specific requirements that a generic deed package can miss. Maintain dated delivery evidence and have Texas counsel confirm the closing professional and document package satisfy the applicable provisions. A purchase-money residential mortgage generally falls outside the federal rescission right under 12 CFR § 1026.23(f)(1), but that does not eliminate state remedies or cure other federal disclosure defects. Avoid promising one universal cancellation period. For an illustrative $20,000 buyer deposit, retain sufficient transaction liquidity until delivery, funding, and applicable cancellation conditions are resolved. If a valid refund obligation arises after the operator spent $15,000 on unrelated acquisitions, accounting profit offers no defense against a cash shortfall. Track the refund exposure separately from recognized spread.

The seventh and eighth traps are counting all collected cash as revenue and believing the property substitutes for defensible servicing records. Split each buyer payment into principal, interest, tax and insurance escrow, authorized fees, and any suspense amount. The retained interest spread is distinct from principal recovery and fiduciary or custodial balances. Likewise, a down payment may contain amounts needed to cure arrears, pay settlement expenses, fund reserves, or satisfy refund conditions; cash receipt alone does not establish earned upfront spread. Have the accountant document recognition under the applicable accounting framework, including principal-versus-agent analysis where relevant. Do not apply a second retained-share haircut to the canonical figures, which already exclude underlying home value and pass-through debt service. Preserve the executed note, security instrument, endorsements, assignments, payment history, and custody trail. UCC § 3-301 concerns entitlement to enforce qualifying negotiable instruments; state enactments, instrument language, and mortgage law determine the actual enforcement route. A scanned PDF does not universally replace custody of the original paper note. Stop secondary sales when chain-of-title or payment representations cannot be substantiated. Contractual repurchase demands can reverse months of spread through principal reimbursement, accrued amounts, and negotiated expense recovery.

sections.heading: 3. Audit Cash at Both Loans and Stress the Owner-Profit Cases
paragraphs: The ninth trap is monitoring the wrap receipt while ignoring the underlying mortgage. Use a licensed third-party servicer authorized for the jurisdiction and product, with a contract that allocates senior payments, escrow administration, statements, complaints, and exception handling. Obtain seller-authorized access or delivery of senior statements without impersonating the borrower or sharing credentials improperly. Reconcile three independent records: cleared buyer receipts, the servicer's allocation ledger, and the senior lender's posted payment. A servicer disbursement confirmation alone does not prove correct lender application. Set internal alerts when a scheduled senior payment lacks posting evidence two business days after its expected posting date, when any escrow balance becomes negative, or when a notice reports delinquency despite a successful disbursement. These are chosen operating thresholds, not statutory grace periods. ACH returns, partial payments, reversals, and suspense allocations require separate exception queues. A $1,650 buyer payment less $1,150 senior principal and interest, $350 tax and insurance provision, and $35 servicing cost leaves $115 in cash before other costs. That cash residual is not automatically retained interest revenue: both loans' principal components must still be separated. Never market the $500 headline difference as spendable monthly profit.

The tenth trap is treating foreclosure carrying cost as a remote legal bill rather than a liquidity schedule. Model missed receipts, senior debt service, insurance, taxes, preservation, counsel, sale expenses, and recovery timing separately. Six months at $1,500 of unavoidable property carrying cost consumes $9,000; add $7,000 of legal and preservation expense and the illustrative workout requires $16,000 before any recovery. A $10,000 reserve covers only 62.5% of that stress budget. If the senior payment continues while the buyer defaults, that reserve cannot be replaced by a spreadsheet receivable. Track delinquency buckets, broken payment promises, returned debits, legal milestones, and liquid unrestricted cash against each property's next obligations. Choose a minimum six-month carrying reserve plus a separately priced workout allowance as an internal starting policy, then increase it for slower jurisdictions and concentrated portfolios. Apply applicable servicing, notice, loss-mitigation, and foreclosure requirements before enforcement; Regulation X obligations depend on coverage and any relevant exemptions. Do not improvise lockouts or utility shutoffs. A workout may preserve more value than immediate enforcement, but modifications require a documented affordability analysis, senior-loan protection, and an updated net recovery comparison.

The eleventh trap is using scale to hide negative exception economics. The canonical Conservative case is $100,000 annual operator revenue at 28% margin, producing $28,000 owner profit and $72,000 implied costs with 1 FT plus 3 C. Base is $475,000 at 40.0%, producing $190,000 and $285,000 implied costs with the same team. Scaled is $850,000 at 52%, producing $442,000 and $408,000 implied costs with 2 FT plus 4 C. These revenue figures comprise net upfront spreads and retained wrap interest margin, not property value, loan principal, or total borrower remittances. Reconcile monthly reports to those definitions before comparing margins. As a separate sensitivity, one unrecovered $16,000 workout expense reduces Base profit to $174,000 and margin to approximately 36.63% if revenue and all other costs remain unchanged. It does not replace the canonical Base case. Track exception cost per active note, reserve coverage, refund liabilities, and concentration by senior lender, servicer, jurisdiction, and maturity month. Pause acquisitions when required reserves are unfunded or existing exceptions lack accountable owners. Automation should expose discrepancies faster; it must not permit one employee to change payment instructions, approve disbursement, and certify the same reconciliation.

sections.heading: 4. Replace Deceptive Acquisition Shortcuts with Measurable Private Offers
paragraphs: The twelfth trap is turning public-record access into an official-looking collection scheme. The mapped play public_filing_trigger_mail_arbitrage uses daily Secretary of State new-LLC filings and County Recorder deed or mortgage recordings to identify timely private offers. Its legitimate products include recurring workplace compliance updates, property-tax appeal contingency services, and exclusive new-mover or B2B introductions. It does not authorize fake government poster invoices, deed-copy bills, invented citations, or implied mandatory purchases. Under 39 U.S.C. § 3001(d), solicitations styled as bills or invoices face specific nonmailability rules unless statutory conditions are met; other provisions address misleading governmental connections. California Business and Professions Code § 17537.9 separately regulates covered recorded-document copy solicitations. Use unambiguous private commercial branding and describe the actual optional service before its price. A new deed can represent an ordinary purchase, estate transfer, or internal reorganization, not distress or permission to infer personal hardship. Validate event types and recipient relevance before sending. For subject-to sourcing, keep acquisition offers separate from subscription invoices and tax-appeal proposals. Never claim the recorder, lender, or state agency selected the recipient for your offer. The fallback is a clearly private letter that accurately states why the service may be useful.

Operate the trigger pipeline with permitted feeds, documented data rights, and limited retention. Deduplicate by jurisdiction, recording identifier, property, and mailing address; suppress prior opt-outs and returned addresses before a Lob or PostGrid API submission. Public availability does not override source terms, privacy requirements, or a provider's acceptable-use rules. Do not evade blocked access, rotate accounts after suspension, or submit a deceptive creative through a different print vendor. Archive the exact letter version, source event, suppression decision, batch identifier, and delivery outcome. Consider an illustrative 1,000-piece batch costing $1.20 per delivered attempt, or $1,200. At a 2% qualified response rate, 20 responses and a 25% response-to-customer conversion produce five customers and $240 postage-only acquisition cost each. A genuine $300 annual update subscription with $120 direct fulfillment cost contributes $180 before acquisition overhead, leaving a $60 first-year deficit per customer before data, staff, refunds, and payment fees. Recurrence helps only if renewal is earned and measured. Pause that cohort rather than claiming positive lifetime value from unsupported retention. For property-tax appeals, recognize contingent fees only when earned under the contract and applicable rules, not when a homeowner submits an inquiry.

The thirteenth trap is mistaking deliverability for permission and response for durable contribution. Instrument complaint rate, opt-out completion, address failure, refund demand, chargeback exposure, and cohort contribution separately. Any substantiated government-impersonation complaint warrants an immediate batch pause and creative review; any unsuppressed opt-out requires correcting the pipeline before the next submission. Use an internal returned-mail investigation threshold above 5% of a mature batch, while acknowledging that provider enforcement uses its own rules and evidence. A vendor can suspend or terminate service for deceptive content or account abuse even when postage was paid. Preserve records and appeal through the vendor's established process, not replacement identities. For exclusive lead monetization, document authorized sharing, the permitted recipient, and exclusivity; never resell the same exclusive lead and conceal the duplication. Keep subscription and lead economics outside the wrap scorecard unless the reporting perimeter explicitly includes them. This chapter's mapped-play analysis supplies a controlled sourcing alternative, not extra revenue silently added to $475,000 Base operator revenue. The final circuit-breaker is simple: stop the activity causing the defect, preserve evidence, fund existing obligations, and resume only after a responsible reviewer verifies the correction against the actual file.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #35, Subject-To & Wraparound Note Arbitrage, holds Rank #09 of 36 with a 90/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its sourcing advantage is finding transferable economics before competing buyers price them, not hiding ownership changes from lenders. This chapter translates 11 mapped plays into a disciplined pipeline: municipal distress signals, recorded debt, seller intent, buyer demand, and professional referrals. Separate property acquisition from mortgage origination, route owner-occupant buyers through a licensed RMLO, and verify every underlying payment through a licensed servicer. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $28,000 Conservative, $190,000 Base, and $442,000 Scaled. Build toward the first three completed transactions before expanding toward ten; track seller permissions, documented debt economics, buyer repayment capacity, and cash reserves rather than celebrating unqualified lead counts.

sections.heading: 1. Mine Debt and Property Events Before Buying Another Lead List
paragraphs: Start with one county, two adjacent postal areas, and a property type your title company, insurance broker, and servicer already understand. Build a parcel-centered ledger in Airtable or PostgreSQL with parcel identifier, recorded owner, mailing address, deed date, mortgage recording date, lien events, permit status, and source timestamp. Pull county recorder indexes, assessor ownership exports, municipal inspection results, and court foreclosure dockets through permitted downloads. A recorded mortgage amount is historical principal, not today's payoff; a recording year suggests a rate cohort but does not establish the contract rate. Require a seller-authorized current statement before scoring debt economics. Cross-reference expired listings through an authorized broker relationship rather than scraping restricted MLS screens. Deduplicate by parcel and owner before spending on enrichment. Exclude active bankruptcy cases pending specialist review, properties beyond your repair capacity, and situations where statutory foreclosure-rescue restrictions defeat the proposed approach. The useful signal is a solvable mismatch: affordable existing debt, a seller needing a timely exit, manageable property defects, and buyers whose documented income supports the eventual payment. Cheap debt without transferable operating economics is simply an attractive line in a spreadsheet. Record source permissions alongside each import so a vendor change does not erase provenance.

Implement municipal_code_violation_trigger_arbitrage as a narrow daily exception queue, not a citywide scraping campaign. Poll municipal building department portals and county recorder dockets for failed structural or fire inspections, expired permits, new code citations, and newly filed mechanic's liens. Join events to parcels, suppress duplicate notices, and distinguish an open violation from a cured case. A lien filing is an allegation requiring document review, not proof that every claimed dollar is collectible. An illustrative weekly batch of 100 events might yield 25 unique properties, eight reachable owners, three authorized assessments, and one viable acquisition conversation. At $250 for permitted data and research, that is $10 per unique property and $250 per acquisition conversation before labor. With owner permission, route the remediation track exclusively to one qualified contractor or construction attorney while separately documenting any acquisition interest. Do not receive a percentage of legal fees or disguise settlement-service referrals as data sales. Treat any separate remediation revenue as outside this volume's scorecard. When portal access is restricted or rate-limited, use low-frequency scheduled API or bulk exports. Identify every message as private commercial contractor or remediation assistance; never imitate an inspector, municipality, or court.

Use eleven mapped plays as operating queues, with the required municipal play and ten chapter-specific sourcing workflows shown below. These workflow labels describe execution rather than additional canonical identifiers. Rate each queue by verified conversations per research hour, not the dramatic appearance of its distress signal. Low-equity owners with current payments can be better counterparties than owners facing tomorrow's auction because there is time for title, disclosures, buyer underwriting, and lender review. Mechanic's liens and failed inspections usually belong in a remediation-first queue until release costs and repair scope are established. Interview three local agents and two property managers about homes that attract payment-sensitive buyers but stall under ordinary financing. Ask for property characteristics and transaction bottlenecks, not protected-class profiles. Build a small inbound page explaining existing-debt purchases, potential lender acceleration, seller credit exposure, and the documents needed for evaluation. Give sellers a choice between a conventional sale referral, a documented creative-finance review, and no further contact. Public-record distress never establishes permission for unrestricted calling or texting. Keep acquisition outreach separate from mortgage advertising, and have the RMLO review any advertised credit terms before publication. Review queue performance every Friday and stop funding channels that produce inaccessible documents rather than usable seller decisions.

callout.title: Win the Document Race Rather Than the Distress Race
callout.body: Prioritize verified debt and repair facts that competing cash-offer campaigns rarely obtain.
items: Save both the original municipal event and its latest disposition; a cured violation should not keep generating distress messages.
Ask for the mortgage statement before discussing a purchase premium; a recent refinance can erase the presumed low-rate advantage.
Have a contractor price the inspection failure separately from cosmetic improvements so a repair budget does not bury a life-safety issue.
Offer the seller a secure, revocable document-sharing invitation rather than requesting mortgage statements through ordinary text messages.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify Both Sides Before Calling a Spread Profitable
paragraphs: Apply a 100-point seller-and-property score only after basic ownership and contact permissions are established. Allocate 25 points to verified debt economics, 20 to title and transfer feasibility, 20 to buyer-supported affordability, 15 to property condition, 10 to seller objectives, and 10 to reserves and exit liquidity. Advance scores of 80 or more, request specific missing evidence at 65 through 79, and archive lower scores unless a documented fact changes. These thresholds are internal priorities, not statistical predictions. A hard stop overrides every score: unresolved authority, an unmanageable lien, unsafe occupancy, unsupported repayment capacity, or inadequate acceleration reserves cannot be offset by a low interest rate. Have title counsel inspect the mortgage, deed restrictions, junior liens, tax balances, association claims, and any foreclosure timetable. The Garn-St Germain framework generally permits enforcement of due-on-sale clauses subject to enumerated exceptions; an ordinary investor acquisition does not become protected merely because payments remain current. Do not use a trust as a concealment device. Identify whether lender consent, a permitted assumption, payoff, or another documented structure can solve the transfer issue. If it cannot, price the exposure explicitly or decline. Record who reviewed the proposed structure and which documents support their conclusion.

Build buyer demand before locking scarce reserves into inventory, but do not confuse a large down payment with repayment capacity. Route every owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO under the applicable SAFE Act, state licensing, and Dodd-Frank Ability-to-Repay framework. Counsel and the RMLO should identify which creditor duties and seller-financing provisions apply; the chapter's operating standard uses licensed underwriting even when a narrow exclusion might otherwise be available. Collect application data through the licensed workflow, obtain appropriate authorization for consumer reports, and avoid storing Social Security numbers in the marketing CRM. Evaluate verified income, employment where relevant, obligations, credit history, mortgage-related expenses, and the applicable payment calculation. Apply consistent criteria and handle adverse-action duties through the responsible creditor. Build demand maps from payment ranges, property needs, and timing, not ethnicity, disability, familial status, or neighborhood proxies for protected characteristics. Ask the RMLO for de-identified counts of completed, supportable files rather than raw applicant records. A pipeline of five documented households at an affordable total housing payment is more useful than fifty people clicking seller-finance advertisements. Refresh capacity before contracting because debt, employment, insurance costs, and property taxes can change between inquiry and closing.

Test the spread using amortization rather than subtracting two advertised interest rates. Illustratively, an underlying $240,000 balance at 3% with 360 monthly payments has principal-and-interest payments of about $1,012. A $270,000 wrap at 7.5% over the same term produces about $1,888. The roughly $876 monthly payment difference is not retained interest revenue: first-month interest is $1,687.50 on the wrap and $600 on the underlying loan, a $1,087.50 interest difference, while principal amortization explains the remaining distinction. Servicing, losses, carrying costs, and operating expenses further affect cash and profit. Add taxes, insurance, association charges, and lawful escrow treatment to the buyer's affordability analysis. Obtain actual insurance quotes for the ownership and occupancy structure; preserving an unsuitable old policy is not a savings strategy. For a $30,000 buyer down payment, $12,000 seller equity, $4,000 arrears, and $4,000 transaction costs leave a $10,000 provisional upfront economic spread before accounting classification. Allocating another $6,000 to reserves leaves $4,000 deployable cash, not a second expense or additional revenue. Have the accountant distinguish sale economics, financing principal, restricted cash, and recognized operator spreads. Replace every illustrative input with closing documents before approving an offer. Stress the exit against both buyer default and lender acceleration.

sections.heading: 3. Run a Permission-Aware Cadence That Converts Documents into Offers
paragraphs: Use a six-touch, twenty-one-day cadence only where each channel is lawful and the recipient has not opted out. Day one is a plain mailed letter naming your company, property, private commercial purpose, and document-review offer. Day three is a manually placed call after applicable do-not-call screening and state-law review. Day seven is a short email where an address was properly obtained, with accurate sender information and an effective unsubscribe process. Day ten is a useful follow-up explaining what a current mortgage statement reveals. Day fourteen offers a fifteen-minute comparison of conventional sale, assumption if available, and existing-debt acquisition. Day twenty-one closes the sequence and offers a clear stop-contact choice. Do not treat a public telephone number as permission for automated dialing, prerecorded messages, or marketing texts. Use Twilio only after a documented channel-specific review and required permissions; use the CRM to enforce suppression across vendors. For inbound demand, publish one factual local case walkthrough and a secure intake form rather than promising universal qualification. Keep credit advertisements under RMLO review, including Regulation Z triggering-term requirements. A channel that creates complaints faster than qualified files is expensive even when its nominal response rate looks impressive.

Model conversion with an explicit denominator. An illustrative cohort of 300 unique researched owners might produce 240 deliverable, eligible contacts, 36 two-way conversations, 18 document-complete seller files, nine fully screened opportunities, six written offers, four signed purchase agreements, and three closings. That equals 80% contact eligibility, 15% conversation conversion from eligible contacts, 50% document completion from conversations, and 1% closing conversion from raw records. A signed purchase agreement is an intermediate milestone, not booked revenue; a referral mandate also does not transfer property. At $1,500 of data and outreach spend, acquisition marketing cost is $500 per closing before labor, legal work, inspections, and failed-file costs. Label these figures as planning hypotheses until your own cohorts mature. Track cohorts by first-contact month and source so a long closing cycle does not make this week's channel look ineffective. Three closings from 300 records does not mean ten closings require exactly 1,000 records; seller mix, title defects, buyer capacity, and reserves can change conversion materially. Review document-completion and offer-acceptance rates separately. If conversations are healthy but statements never arrive, fix trust and secure intake before purchasing more records. Never scale marketing faster than the underwriting team's document review capacity.

Handle objections by clarifying the actual exposure, not by winning a debate. When a seller asks whether the loan leaves their name, answer that a subject-to transfer ordinarily leaves their existing borrower obligation in place unless the lender releases it. Offer payment visibility and independent review, not a promise of release. When asked whether the lender can call the loan, explain the due-on-sale clause, applicable law, and the transaction's documented response plan. If a seller demands all retail equity immediately, compare conventional sale proceeds rather than forcing an unsuitable structure. If a buyer asks to qualify solely through a deposit, explain that licensed repayment-capacity review still applies. If a contractor wants an exclusive lead, establish owner permission, service scope, response time, and any lawful fixed-price work separately from mortgage settlement referrals. Record the objection category and the next evidence-producing action in the CRM. A respectful decline with a specific reason is a useful outcome because it preserves time and prevents unsuitable commitments. Follow every substantive call with a written summary of discussed alternatives, requested records, and unresolved risks. Avoid scripts claiming government affiliation, guaranteed credit repair, hidden lender protection, or inevitable foreclosure savings. Those claims undermine the very trust required to obtain reliable documents.

sections.heading: 4. Land Three Controlled Closings, Then Earn the Right to Pursue Ten
paragraphs: Sequence the first two to six months around evidence, not an arbitrary closing quota. During weeks one and two, engage local real-estate counsel, title or escrow, a licensed RMLO, an insurance broker, and a third-party servicer licensed where required. Confirm who can actually support wrap transactions; a familiar company name does not establish jurisdictional capability. During weeks three through six, work the first researched cohort and build parallel buyer intake. During weeks seven through twelve, advance the strongest files through inspections, underwriting, disclosures, and closing preparation. Months four through six should concentrate on verified servicing performance and a second cohort only when reserves remain adequate. Three completed transactions are a practical initial target; reaching ten within this window requires unusually strong conversion, capacity, and capital, rather than a different definition of a win. Distinguish signed agreements, completed acquisitions, completed wrap sales, and performing boarded notes on the dashboard. Some transactions will not close in the window. A file that exits to an ordinary sale can validate your sourcing relationship without generating wrap revenue. Do not count it in this volume's retained-interest production. Assign each live file a next action, accountable person, and dated dependency so outside professionals are not mistaken for available full-time staff.

Keep the Formula v2.0 scenarios fixed while treating sourcing volumes as illustrative support. Conservative annual operator revenue is $100,000, expenses are $72,000, and owner net profit is $28,000 at 28% with 1 FT + 3 C. Base revenue is $475,000, expenses are $285,000, and owner profit is $190,000 at 40.0% with 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled revenue is $850,000, expenses are $408,000, and owner profit is $442,000 at 52% with 2 FT + 4 C. One arithmetic bridge is ten recognized upfront spreads averaging $4,000 plus twenty performing note-year equivalents averaging $3,000 of retained interest for Conservative; twenty-five times $7,000 plus fifty times $6,000 for Base; and forty times $10,000 plus seventy-five times $6,000 for Scaled. These are illustrative revenue mixes, not additional scorecard inputs or first-year promises. A note-year equivalent represents twelve months of recognized contribution, so midyear closings contribute fractionally. Despite the scorecard's gross-revenue label, its basis already excludes property face value, loan principal, and pass-through debt service. Preserve that retained-share basis without taking the spread twice. Have the accountant apply ASC 606 where applicable to fee or sale components and the relevant lending guidance to interest; cash collection alone does not determine recognized revenue.

Board each closed wrap with a documented payment waterfall and monthly reconciliation of buyer receipts, underlying debt service, taxes, insurance, servicing charges, reserves, and operator distributions. Autopay is a collection mechanism, not evidence that the underlying lender was paid. Obtain servicer reports and independently verify the underlying account through authorized access or statements; investigate differences before distributing cash. Keep buyer defaults and underlying-payment failures in separate exception queues because one can occur without the other. Reconfirm escrow sufficiency after tax reassessments and insurance renewals. For Texas transactions, review Property Code Section 5.016 alongside Finance Code Chapter 159, including applicable licensing, disclosures, borrower rights, and payment obligations; one notice provision does not cover the entire structure. Review federal servicing requirements and state collection procedures with the servicer before drafting default messages. Reserve planning should use actual local foreclosure timelines, repair exposure, and an acceleration-response model, not merely six scheduled installments. The $12,000–$65,000 startup range and $2,000–$12,000 monthly operating range do not authorize thin property reserves or replace the annual scenario expense totals. Increase sourcing only after the first three transactions demonstrate clean document retention, timely underlying payments, and accurate revenue classification. A performing note with transparent servicing is the repeatable product; an impressive closing photograph is not.

sections.heading: 1. Convert eleven operating plays into a verified acquisition queue
paragraphs: Treat intake as evidence collection, not permission to acquire a property. The eleven mapped operating plays used here are debt-trigger sourcing, county-roll ingestion, comparable-equity screening, property-tax appeal execution, seller authorization, title and lien verification, underlying-loan verification, RMLO buyer underwriting, escrow closing, licensed-servicer boarding, and cash reconciliation. These are chapter-local workflow labels; the supplied catalog identifier is property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency. Keep its TRACK_1 work order separate from the note acquisition order. Pull authorized county assessor exports when annual notices appear, then attach parcel identifiers, notice dates, protest deadlines, assessed values, homestead status, and comparable sales. Record the source URL and retrieval timestamp before scoring anything. A low mortgage coupon is attractive only after the unpaid balance, arrears, escrow shortage, maturity, and transfer terms survive verification. Seller permission to obtain statements does not transfer the loan or release the seller from liability. Assign every lead a stable source key and every subsequent decision an immutable event key. The owner handles exceptions; contractors collect documents, underwrite buyers, and service loans within their actual authority. Reject unsupported balances rather than converting estimates into acquisition economics or marketing claims about immediate available equity.

Use the assessment appeal as a measured intervention, not a reason to buy a defective title. An automated valuation model should compare assessment-to-supported-market-value ratios within defensible property classes, neighborhoods, size bands, and condition groups. A parcel assessed at $300,000 against supported value of $250,000 has a 1.20 ratio; neighbors near 1.00 justify investigation, not an automatic reduction. If an accepted assessment change reduces the actual first-year tax bill from $12,000 to $7,200, the verified saving is $4,800. A 40% contingency produces $1,920, within the specified 30–50% range. Calculate the saving from the issued bill or refund after applicable exemptions and rates, not merely from the valuation difference. In Texas, calendar Tax Code §41.44 deadlines and evaluate unequal-appraisal evidence under §41.43 with the authorized representative. Partner with licensed local property-tax consultants or attorneys of record wherever required; automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing only through permitted county channels. Capture submission receipts, parcel-level exceptions, and engagement authority. If the AVM fails validation, route to manual comparables or withdraw before incurring representation costs. The worked cohort excludes appeal fees entirely, preventing speculative savings from inflating the Base case.

Price the acquisition around verified obligations and a funded failure path. Obtain the note, deed of trust or mortgage, current statement, payment history, reinstatement quote where relevant, tax certificate, insurance declarations, and title commitment through authorized channels. A subject-to conveyance generally leaves the existing borrower obligated; a wrap adds another obligation rather than substituting the buyer for that borrower. Under 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3, lenders generally may enforce contractual due-on-sale clauses, subject to enumerated exceptions. An ordinary investor transfer does not become protected merely because a trust or servicing arrangement appears in the documents. Record the acceleration exposure and a priced refinance, payoff, consensual unwind, or sale strategy before committing capital. For illustration, a $1,500 monthly underlying payment plus $500 of taxes and insurance creates $2,000 monthly carrying exposure; a three-month interruption needs $6,000 before collection, repair, or foreclosure costs. Do not label that liquidity reserve an expense when it is merely transferred between operator accounts. A written investment policy should reject transactions whose acceleration or buyer-default exposure exceeds available capital. The stated $12,000–$65,000 startup range is a planning envelope, not proof that every candidate property fits it.

sections.heading: 2. Install six atomic production modules before moving money
paragraphs: The reference implementation below is a deliberately bounded SQLite operator-contribution ledger, not a substitute for a licensed servicer's borrower, trust, escrow, or amortization system. Copy its six cells into the named files in one project directory. Initialize with sqlite3 ledger.sqlite < schema.sql, then install the reporting views with sqlite3 ledger.sqlite < reports.sql. Feed each Python command one JSON object on standard input. Use integer cents, stable business identifiers, and source-issued settlement references. Intake scoring prioritizes review; it never constitutes credit approval. The workflow records independently verified evidence, while cash posting accepts only earned, settled operator amounts. Gross borrower receipts, refundable deposits, escrow balances, and principal belong in the servicing system and are excluded here. A separate general ledger must handle accruals, deferred amounts, depreciation, entity taxes, and other entries outside this restricted cash-contribution model. Financial reporting should classify interest under applicable lending guidance and assess principal-versus-agent presentation for relevant service revenue under ASC 606; neither permits calling house value revenue. Back up the database using SQLite's backup API and retain immutable source exports in encrypted storage with access limited to the assigned transaction team.

Concurrency is controlled inside the stated boundary: every application write opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the same local database, validates the current record, and commits one complete transaction. UNIQUE constraints protect source keys, event keys, and settlement references. Canonical payload comparison distinguishes a safe retry from a conflicting reuse of an identifier. A repeated request either returns its previous outcome or fails explicitly; it cannot silently post twice. Workflow updates additionally compare the expected state and require exactly one affected row. Journal rows express balanced double-entry amounts in a single immutable record, eliminating an intermediate half-posted journal. WAL mode supports readers while SQLite serializes writers. Keep the database on a supported local filesystem, not a shared network mount. Multiple application hosts require a properly implemented transactional database service rather than copied database files. These controls remove application-level check-then-write races for cooperating local writers; they do not make external banking or servicer APIs exactly-once. No module sends payments. Import independently confirmed settlements after external execution, preserving the provider's reference. A future payment integration needs provider idempotency, an outbox, and explicit recovery after uncertain responses before it can safely automate disbursement.

Operate the scripts behind an authenticated work queue rather than exposing raw JSON submission to sellers or buyers. Boolean verification fields represent an authorized reviewer's recorded conclusions, not self-certifying customer claims. Attach the reviewed evidence bundle identifier to every transition and retain its hash and reviewer identity in the surrounding document system. The reserve transition records settled escrow evidence; it does not create or verify a bank transfer by itself. Before production, restrict database writes to this service account and test replay, collision, illegal transition, missing bank control, and interrupted-transaction cases. The independent bank control must come from an accountant's normalized statement export, never from the ledger totals it is supposed to test. Normalization removes transfers and segregated servicing flows while preserving a bridge back to the complete statement. Each month, also reconcile servicer collections, underlying principal and interest, tax disbursements, insurance payments, and suspense balances outside this narrow ledger. The supplied QA command checks structural integrity and operator cash differences; it cannot establish borrower affordability or prove that a lender accepted a payment. Require those independent checks before labeling the monthly package complete.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
import sys

data = json.load(sys.stdin)
required = (
    "case_key", "source_key", "coupon_bps",
    "arrears_cents", "reserve_required_cents"
)
if any(key not in data for key in required):
    raise ValueError("Provide every required intake field")
for key in ("case_key", "source_key"):
    if not isinstance(data[key], str) or not data[key].strip():
        raise ValueError("Business identifiers must contain text")
for key in ("coupon_bps", "arrears_cents", "reserve_required_cents"):
    if type(data[key]) is not int or data[key] < 0:
        raise ValueError("Rate and monetary inputs require nonnegative integers")
if data["reserve_required_cents"] <= 0:
    raise ValueError("Set a positive reviewed reserve requirement")

score = 30
score += 40 if data["coupon_bps"] <= 450 else 10
score += 20 if data["arrears_cents"] == 0 else 0
payload = json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
db = sqlite3.connect("ledger.sqlite", timeout=10, isolation_level=None)
db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
try:
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    prior = db.execute(
        "SELECT id, intake_payload FROM case_file WHERE case_key=?",
        (data["case_key"],)
    ).fetchone()
    if prior:
        if prior[1] != payload:
            raise ValueError("Case identifier reused with conflicting intake")
        result = prior[0]
    else:
        cursor = db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO case_file "
            "(case_key, source_key, intake_payload, score, "
            "reserve_required_cents, state) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'SCORED')",
            (
                data["case_key"], data["source_key"], payload,
                score, data["reserve_required_cents"]
            )
        )
        result = cursor.lastrowid
    db.execute("COMMIT")
    print(json.dumps({"case_id": result, "review_priority_score": score}))
except Exception:
    if db.in_transaction:
        db.execute("ROLLBACK")
    raise
finally:
    db.close()
Stable source identifiers prevent repeated imports from creating duplicate acquisitions
Conflicting payloads fail explicitly instead of overwriting previously reviewed evidence

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_monthly AS
SELECT
    period,
    SUM(revenue_cents) AS revenue_cents,
    SUM(expense_cents) AS expense_cents,
    SUM(cash_cents) AS net_cash_cents
FROM journal
GROUP BY period;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_reconciliation AS
WITH periods AS (
    SELECT period FROM journal
    UNION
    SELECT period FROM bank_control
)
SELECT
    p.period,
    COALESCE(m.revenue_cents, 0) AS revenue_cents,
    COALESCE(m.expense_cents, 0) AS expense_cents,
    COALESCE(m.net_cash_cents, 0) AS ledger_cash_cents,
    b.net_cash_cents AS bank_cash_cents,
    CASE WHEN b.period IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE COALESCE(m.net_cash_cents, 0) - b.net_cash_cents
    END AS difference_cents,
    CASE
        WHEN b.period IS NULL THEN 'Independent bank control required'
        WHEN COALESCE(m.net_cash_cents, 0) != b.net_cash_cents
            THEN 'Investigate operator cash reconciliation difference'
        ELSE 'Operator cash agrees with independent statement control'
    END AS reconciliation_status
FROM periods p
LEFT JOIN v_monthly m ON m.period = p.period
LEFT JOIN bank_control b ON b.period = p.period;

FROM journal WHERE revenue_cents != 0

FROM journal WHERE expense_cents != 0;

sections.heading: 3. Close, board, collect, and investigate exceptions without obscuring obligations
paragraphs: For every owner-occupant wrap in this operating model, engage a licensed RMLO before promising terms or collecting nonrefundable origination money. Verify the originator through NMLS Consumer Access and confirm the relevant state authority, entity coverage, and activity scope. The SAFE Act framework includes 12 U.S.C. §5103; loan-originator requirements and limited seller-financer exclusions also appear in 12 CFR §1026.36. Do not turn an exclusion into a blanket exemption from other lending duties. Determine the applicable creditor, loan, and transaction coverage, then document repayment capacity under 12 CFR §1026.43 where required. Keep verified income, assets, employment, debts, credit obligations, payment calculations, and underwriting conclusions in the protected loan file. Underwrite the buyer's full scheduled housing burden, including taxes, insurance, association dues, and any balloon exposure, rather than the operator's desired spread. The underwriting decision must precede closing and survive independent file review. If the buyer fails, stop that buyer's transaction; do not replace missing income verification with a larger down payment or relabel an owner-occupied purchase as business-purpose credit. A different qualified buyer, a conventional sale, or withdrawal is the operating fallback, with each alternative repriced against actual carrying costs.

Escrow instructions should connect seller disclosures, underlying lien information, buyer documents, recorded security instruments, insurance interests, and payment routing in one closing checklist. For Texas property, evaluate Property Code §5.016, including required notice contents, timing, delivery, and applicable exceptions; separately evaluate Finance Code Chapter 159 for wrap mortgage lending requirements. Do not assume one disclosure satisfies the other regime. Have the closing professional confirm the applicable delivery calendar before scheduling signatures. Insurance must reflect actual ownership, occupancy, lender interests, and the transaction structure; an old policy left untouched can create a serious coverage dispute. Confirm tax escrow responsibility without collecting the same obligation through two incompatible channels. Board the licensed third-party servicer using executed documents, amortization schedules, underlying loan information, payment permissions, tax and insurance instructions, and a tested reporting destination. Require written boarding acceptance. The operator must never substitute an internal spreadsheet for proof that the underlying lender received payment. If recording, funding, or boarding fails, preserve escrow restrictions and use the closing professional's documented correction process. No script in this chapter authorizes escrow release, alters borrower rights, or cures a missed statutory notice.

Run collections through the servicer, but keep exception ownership inside the operator team. Each month match borrower receipts to contractual allocations, underlying lender credits, escrow movements, fees, principal changes, and retained interest. A $2,000 borrower receipt is not $2,000 of operator revenue when most funds satisfy another obligation. Export the actual retained amount only after the waterfall and settlement agree. Configure alerts for returned payments, lender-side posting delays, insurance cancellation notices, tax delinquency, maturity changes, and unexplained suspense balances. A buyer default requires a dated contact and resolution log, applicable notices, and state-specific enforcement work; it does not permit self-help possession or improvised eviction. Where applicable, 12 CFR §1024.41 restricts foreclosure timing and establishes loss mitigation procedures, including the general 120-day delinquency threshold subject to its conditions and exceptions. Reserve enough liquidity to keep underlying obligations current while the lawful process runs. If the underlying lender accelerates, activate the documented payoff or refinance response and recalculate cash needs immediately. Report an interrupted spread as an interrupted spread. Do not smooth missing collections into reported revenue merely because the annual scorecard assumes a performing portfolio and a target level of production.

sections.heading: 4. Walk a 90-day replacement cohort into the exact Base run rate
paragraphs: The cohort is an established operator's replacement-production exercise, not a claim that a startup creates a seasoned portfolio in ninety days. Begin with forty performing wrap positions and replenish scheduled exits so the average performing exposure remains forty note-years annually. Each position contributes an illustrative $5,000 annual retained interest margin after underlying interest pass-through, producing $200,000 annually. Actual servicing schedules must support that amount; principal amortization and property value are excluded. Separately, twenty-five annual placements retain $11,000 each, producing $275,000. One illustrative closing receives $18,000 of buyer funds and applies $7,000 to seller and direct settlement allocations, leaving $11,000 earned operator spread; escrow verifies the contractual entitlement and excludes refundable amounts. Together, $275,000 plus $200,000 equals exactly $475,000 of canonical revenue. The quarter closes one, two, and three replacement placements, with matching departures at month-end. Departing positions supply their final scheduled month; replacements begin the next monthly collection cycle, preventing double-counted interest. This assumes uninterrupted replacement and collections. A missed payment, delayed placement, or vacancy changes actual results and must appear as a variance rather than an invisible adjustment to the target.

Track lead cohorts separately from cash dates. Month 1 receives sixty leads, scrubs forty-eight, completes twelve desk reviews, advances three diligence files, and closes one. Month 2 receives eighty leads, scrubs sixty-four, reviews sixteen, advances five, and closes two. Month 3 receives one hundred leads, scrubs eighty, reviews twenty, advances seven, and closes three. Each cohort closes within its labeled month only because these are prequalified replacement opportunities inside an established pipeline; a new operator should instead expect the stated two-to-six month first-deal interval. The table accounts for every unclosed lead rather than treating review activity as inventory. Failed diligence consumes $1,000, $1,500, and $2,000 respectively, already included in monthly operating outlays. No borrower credit loss occurs in this worked case, and no refundable deposits are counted as receipts. Monthly retained interest is $16,666.67, $16,666.67, and $16,666.66, exactly $50,000 for the quarter. Round at the portfolio reporting level while preserving individual servicer allocations in cents. Closing contribution arrives only after settlement; monthly interest arrives only after the servicer waterfall and bank evidence support the recognized retained amount.

Use $23,750 of monthly all-in operating outlays for this established Base business: $8,000 fixed platform and administrative overhead, $12,000 variable acquisition and production expense, and $3,750 contracted servicing, bookkeeping, and specialist support. The $8,000 fixed component fits the stated $2,000–$12,000 monthly overhead planning range; that range cannot be treated as the entire Base cost base because $475,000 revenue less $190,000 profit requires $285,000 annual expenses. Do not deduct the $7,000 settlement allocation again: it was already removed when deriving each $11,000 retained upfront spread. Quarterly revenue is $116,000, expenses are $71,250, and operating cash contribution is $44,750. This illustration assumes recognized amounts settle within the same month, with no owner distributions or new capital expenditures. A normalized Base quarter has 6.25 placements, $118,750 revenue, and $47,500 profit. The worked quarter is lower by one-quarter placement, or $2,750. Complete nineteen additional placements over the remaining nine months while maintaining forty performing note-years to reach the exact annual Base result. Conservative and Scaled retain their separate canonical margins; neither is inferred by multiplying this short cohort's observed cash margin.

sections.heading: 1. Anchor every opportunity to recorded instruments, not lead-list estimates
paragraphs: Start with a county-specific evidence map before buying a national lead subscription. For each target county, record the recorder's document coverage, assessor parcel format, tax collector billing calendar, foreclosure procedure, and courthouse retrieval route. An assessor identifies taxable property; a recorder indexes instruments; neither establishes a current mortgage balance or insurable title. Link county, parcel identifier, legal description, instrument number, recording date, and source retrieval timestamp. Preserve leading zeros and original owner spellings. Condominium units, parent parcels, and subdivided lots require separate relationship records rather than aggressive address deduplication. A notice of default is a dated procedural event, not evidence that the borrower wants an offer or that a sale remains scheduled. Retrieve the actual notice, then verify postponements and cancellations through the responsible trustee or court. In Texas, nonjudicial sale mechanics under Property Code section 51.002 make timing material; the posted date does not substitute for transaction-specific review. Assign every lead an evidence state: discovered, document retrieved, owner confirmed, debt verified, or executable. Only the final state may enter acquisition cash planning, and that state still requires a current title commitment and transaction-specific closing review.

Use the directory in this section and the next as one sixteen-resource waterfall. Rows one through eight establish public-record provenance; rows nine through sixteen add paid enrichment, regulatory verification, and execution diagnostics. County systems differ, so a named portal is a deployment example, not nationwide coverage. NYC ACRIS supplies recorded property documents for its covered boroughs, while Staten Island requires its separate recording channel. Maricopa recorder and assessor records illustrate why instrument ownership and parcel assessment should be joined without assuming identical refresh schedules. Harris County foreclosure postings are useful event signals, but the trustee remains the source for current sale instructions. Never interpret absence from one index as absence of liens. Federal tax liens, judgments, probate interests, municipal assessments, and bankruptcy proceedings may require separate searches and title examination. Store source coverage explicitly, including counties and years searched. Where a portal provides only a browser interface, use that interface or purchase authorized bulk access; do not manufacture an undocumented scraping entitlement. A restricted portal, broken image link, or missing instrument triggers a clerk request or title-company retrieval, not a guessed field silently carried into an investment memorandum.

Budget retrieval by expected decision value. An illustrative first pass of 400 records at $0.25 each costs $100; reviewing 40 resulting candidates for ten minutes each at $45 per hour adds $300. The $400 screen therefore costs $10 per reviewed candidate before title, underwriting, or closing expenses. These are internal planning assumptions, not quoted vendor prices. Require a written commercial quote before substituting purchased API usage into that model. A recorded $210,000 mortgage from six years ago does not establish today's payoff: modifications, arrears, advances, partial releases, and subordinate liens can reverse apparent equity. Obtain seller-authorized statements, reinstatement figures where relevant, and payoff information with expiration dates through accepted channels. Distinguish an interest rate printed in an original note from an adjustable rate currently effective. The low-rate acquisition thesis survives only if actual payment obligations, insurance, taxes, and acceleration exposure are affordable together. Under 12 U.S.C. 1701j-3, do not assume an ordinary subject-to acquisition or wrap sale falls within a protected transfer exception. If acceleration cannot be absorbed through a documented refinance, payoff, or sale plan, reject the acquisition rather than assigning the risk a zero-dollar spreadsheet value.

callout.title: Buy the missing fact, not another overlapping lead list
callout.body: A veteran desk pays for evidence that changes funding decisions and preserves the chain connecting every number to its source.
items: Order the recorded modification before modeling a low-rate spread; original mortgage metadata can conceal changed maturity or payment terms.
Keep trustee postponement evidence beside the foreclosure notice; a stale sale date can corrupt both outreach priority and cancellation timing.
Store the exact parcel and legal description returned by title; street-address normalization must never merge adjacent collateral.
Separate seller arrears from recurring debt service so a temporary reinstatement burden does not masquerade as permanent monthly margin.

sections.heading: 2. Enrich selectively and verify the people controlling origination and servicing
paragraphs: Design enrichment as a sequence of questions, not a purchase of every field a vendor offers. First resolve parcel identity through county records. Next request property and recorded-mortgage attributes from ATTOM or an alternative contracted provider. Then obtain the specific missing document through DataTree or the recorder. Reserve title examination, borrower underwriting, insurance quotes, and servicing setup for transactions that survive those checks. ATTOM Property API, CoreLogic Trestle, and DataTree serve different access and coverage needs; Trestle is an authorized listing-data channel, not a universal lien registry. BatchData contact enrichment is a lead-contact aid, not proof of ownership or permission to contact someone through every channel. Reject contact matches that cannot be tied to the intended party through an independent signal. Vendor-estimated equity and mortgage balances remain estimates even when delivered through a polished API. Keep separate fields for observed document facts, vendor estimates, seller representations, and verified servicer figures. A field-level source ledger lets the operator replace a weak estimate without erasing the historical basis of an earlier decision. When two providers disagree, request the primary instrument instead of averaging incompatible values into apparent precision.

Verify the originator and servicer before sending an owner-occupant buyer into the workflow. Use NMLS Consumer Access to inspect the individual RMLO, sponsoring company, license status, and relevant state authority; retrieve the underlying state regulator record when the scope is unclear. NMLS identifiers are identifiers, not a universal authorization to perform every activity in every jurisdiction. This desk routes every owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO and documented repayment analysis, while counsel determines the transaction's precise federal and state coverage. Regulation Z section 1026.43 sets ability-to-repay requirements for covered transactions; exemptions and seller-financer provisions require specific analysis rather than slogans about a permitted annual deal count. Texas adds wrap-mortgage requirements under Finance Code Chapter 159, and Property Code section 5.016 addresses specified transfers involving existing liens. Hire a third-party servicer licensed where required, verify that status, and document responsibility for underlying payments, escrow administration, statements, complaints, and exception escalation. A vendor's ability to collect ACH payments does not establish authority to service a particular wrap loan. Obtain a sample report demonstrating both buyer collections and independently verified underlying mortgage disbursements before signing the servicing agreement.

Keep borrower qualification outside the public-record enrichment lake. Income documents, consumer reports, account credentials, and identification belong in restricted systems with purpose-specific access and retention schedules. 15 U.S.C. 1681b governs permissible purposes for consumer reports; a property lead alone does not establish one. Let the authorized RMLO obtain the necessary reports through its established process and return the decision evidence needed for the transaction. Track applicable adverse-action and record-retention responsibilities explicitly rather than assuming the contractor owns every obligation. For outreach, check applicable calling restrictions and suppression requirements before using enriched phone numbers. On the technical side, Postman collections should reference environment-managed credentials, contain synthetic test payloads, and exclude live borrower documents from shared workspaces. A local SQLite ledger can retain source hashes, retrieval timestamps, document identifiers, and reconciliation states without duplicating sensitive files. An illustrative waterfall that screens 100 parcels, purchases 20 document packages, and commissions five title reviews should report spend at each transition. If a package costs an assumed $18, that stage costs $360, not $1,800 across all initial leads. Replace the assumption with contracted pricing and stop purchasing enrichment when the underlying opportunity fails.
